result.notes: Repository files read: 0. No filesystem, worktree, git history, pull-request body, plan or prior analysis was consulted. All probe cases have natural homes under the five independent classifications, so no placement is marked as a forced fit. Missing question: What compatibility, versioning and deprecation guarantees must cross-unit APIs, publicly published packages and embedded artefacts provide, and are releases independent or estate-wide lockstep?

result.design:
Questions answered: What is a unit; when must one thing become two units; where does each unit live; how is it addressed independently of its current path; who owns it; which bytes humans may edit; how it is built, tested, released, deployed, or refreshed; who may consume or redistribute it; what its public boundary is; how it depends on other units; what must change atomically with it; what a newcomer or machine collaborator should inspect first; and how all of those rules are enforced and evolved.

Unit definition: a unit is the smallest independently nameable, human-owned, testable and dependency-addressable body that has one coherent lifecycle contract. Split parts when they have independently meaningful release, deployment, refresh or regeneration triggers; materially different consumers, failure modes, quality gates or operational authority; or a stable interface that permits independent change. Keep parts together when correctness requires atomic change and no stable interface exists. Size, language, framework and file type alone do not create units. Different custody or rights may be represented by protected subtrees inside one coherent unit rather than forcing artificial units.

The design rests on exactly five independent classifications: primary purpose and domain; lifecycle and atomicity; byte custody and provenance; delivery and assurance; and rights and reuse. Dependency position is deliberately not a sixth classification: it is derived from the unit graph. Ownership, framework and popularity do not determine directory placement.

Implied layout: units/<realm>/<domain>/<slug>/ is the only unit shape, with no nested units. Realm is one of apps, libraries, connectors, tooling, operations, studies, data, assets or artifacts. Domain is a controlled problem-space term, and slug is a specific capability name. Each directory contains unit.json and only the relevant conventional roots: src/, tests/, data/curated/, snapshots/<feed>/, vendor/<supplier>/ and generated/<recipe>/. The manifest records a stable path-independent id, owner, summary, lifecycle, custody map, delivery contract, rights map, exports, non-code relations and audience-specific startHere entries. A generated root-level estate-map.json contains every unit's id, path, one-line purpose, owner, entrypoints, exports, rights summary, lifecycle, documentation entrypoints and typed graph edges, allowing discovery with one read or a targeted query.

The graph contains derived TypeScript import edges plus declared non-import edges such as generates, embeds, refreshes-from, reads-data-from and operates-on. Cross-unit imports must use declared exports and stable package aliases; cross-unit relative paths and deep imports are forbidden. Unit-level cycles are rejected: a strongly connected component is evidence that its members form one effective unit or need an explicit interface extraction. Fan-in, fan-out, blast radius, unused exports and dependency layers are graph reports rather than hand-maintained labels.

Failure prevention: machine-owned paths are regenerated in a clean location and byte-compared in CI; vendor snapshots are digest-verified and excluded from formatters. File-touch co-change analysis identifies distant lockstep units, while declared atomic relations make CI reject one-sided changes. Every path resolves to an explicit rights record, restricted-byte fingerprints are indexed, and copying across units must go through a rights-aware operation that records provenance. The generated catalog exposes one canonical start point per unit and audience and suppresses superseded guidance. Policy is executable through schemas, import rules, graph checks, custody verification, rights checks and profile-selected gates rather than depending on prose recall. Stable ids, stable import aliases, graph-derived impact selection and adapters for old public entrypoints allow units to move incrementally without a repository-wide flag day.

Adoption is ratcheted: first register existing roots without moving them, generate the catalog and graph, then forbid new unregistered files, then close custody and dependency violations unit by unit. Moves preserve stable ids and import names. Changed-unit CI runs the unit's declared gates plus graph-selected dependent gates, which keeps enforcement affordable at the stated scale.

organisingRules.name: Classification 1 of 5: purpose address
organisingRules.rule: Classify a unit by its primary role and problem domain, not by framework, team name or current dependency layer. Each unit has exactly one realm, domain and capability slug.
organisingRules.carrier: Directory units/<realm>/<domain>/<slug>/ and matching unit.json fields realm, domain and slug. A schema validates the realm vocabulary, kebab-case names, three-level shape and absence of nested unit manifests.

organisingRules.name: Classification 2 of 5: lifecycle and atomicity
organisingRules.rule: A unit has one accountable human owner and one coherent set of change reasons, triggers, release or refresh mechanism and atomicity requirements. Independent triggers, consumers or failure contracts normally create separate units; inseparable invariants remain together.
organisingRules.carrier: unit.json fields owner and lifecycle.changeReasons, lifecycle.triggers, lifecycle.release, lifecycle.refresh and lifecycle.atomicWith. CI selects gates from these fields and rejects a change that touches only one side of an atomic relation.

organisingRules.name: Classification 3 of 5: byte custody and provenance
organisingRules.rule: Every path is classified as handwritten, curated, externally snapshotted, generated or vendored-byte-preserved. Hand editing is allowed only for handwritten and curated paths. Each other path names its source, recipe and verifier.
organisingRules.carrier: Conventional roots src/, data/curated/, snapshots/<feed>/, generated/<recipe>/ and vendor/<supplier>/ plus unit.json custody path rules. CI clean-builds generated outputs, verifies snapshot and vendor digests, and prevents formatters or ordinary edit workflows from writing protected roots.

organisingRules.name: Classification 4 of 5: delivery and assurance
organisingRules.rule: Purpose does not imply support or quality. Record independently whether a unit is deployed, publicly published, embedded, internal-only or non-shipping; its audience and support promise; its quality profile; and whether it can affect live systems.
organisingRules.carrier: unit.json delivery fields form, audience, support, qualityProfile, publicName and liveSystemAccess. Gate selection is manifest-driven: studies may use product-code gates without shipping, while operations use safety and authority gates without pretending to be product code.

organisingRules.name: Classification 5 of 5: rights and reuse
organisingRules.rule: Every file inherits an explicit SPDX-compatible rights rule, with path overrides for differently licensed data, vendor material and trademarks. Redistribution and copying permission are separate from copyright licence.
organisingRules.carrier: unit.json rights.default and rights.overrides entries containing licence, attribution, redistribution and copyPolicy, with per-file rights sidecars where legally required. CI rejects uncovered or conflicting paths, scans restricted-byte fingerprints, and requires provenance plus owner approval for protected cross-unit copies.

organisingRules.name: Stable identity and naming
organisingRules.rule: A unit's identity and import address survive physical moves. Directory slugs are descriptive kebab-case; stable ids are dot-qualified semantic names; internal package aliases are derived from ids. Public packages may retain externally meaningful names.
organisingRules.carrier: unit.json id and delivery.publicName, generated workspace aliases and estate-map.json path resolution. CI checks global uniqueness and forbids path-relative cross-unit imports.

organisingRules.name: Public boundaries and dependency direction
organisingRules.rule: A consumer may use only another unit's declared exports. Generic libraries cannot depend on product-specific units, operations cannot be imported by product code, and unit cycles are not accepted as normal architecture.
organisingRules.carrier: Exports come from compiler and package metadata reconciled with unit.json exports. Static analysis derives import edges, validates realm constraints and deep-import bans, and condenses strongly connected components for a fail-or-remediate report.

organisingRules.name: Generated and embedded artifact contracts
organisingRules.rule: A generated collection becomes an artifact unit when it has an independent rebuild trigger, retention contract or consumer boundary; otherwise it is a generated subtree of its owning unit. Producer, output owner and serving unit may differ but must be connected explicitly.
organisingRules.carrier: unit.json artifact declarations and typed graph edges generates and embeds. Each declaration names producer id, recipe, inputs, trigger, output path and verifier. CI rebuilds and compares tracked output and follows generated edges during impact selection.

organisingRules.name: Cohesion and change coordination
organisingRules.rule: Repeated symmetric co-change is evidence to colocate, merge or declare an atomic relationship; it is not silently ignored and does not automatically override semantic boundaries.
organisingRules.carrier: A rolling file-touch graph, using paths and timestamps rather than commit messages, reports pairs with at least ten joint changes and more than 80 percent conditional co-change in both directions. Undeclared high-cohesion pairs fail the architecture audit until owners merge them, colocate them or add a reviewed atomicWith relation.

organisingRules.name: Machine-first discovery and canonical guidance
organisingRules.rule: A collaborator should identify the relevant unit, entrypoint, owner, rights and dependency neighborhood without scanning the tree. Each audience has at most one canonical starting resource; superseded material is never presented as current.
organisingRules.carrier: Generated estate-map.json and a query command backed by unit.json summary, startHere and documentation records containing audience, status, supersedes and verifiedAgainst. CI rejects duplicate canonical entries and broken or unregistered references.

organisingRules.name: Executable enforcement and affordable evolution
organisingRules.rule: Organisational rules must be executable and proportional. Changed units run their own gates and graph-selected dependent gates. Reorganisation proceeds by registration and ratcheting rather than a big-bang move.
organisingRules.carrier: A versioned manifest schema and enforcement unit under units/tooling/estate/architecture implement validation, graph construction, rights checks, custody checks and move tooling. Stable ids, generated aliases, compatibility adapters and a declining exception ledger make incremental moves mechanically safe.

probePlacements.placement: Two neighboring units: units/data/<service>/interface-spec-snapshot and units/data/<service>/bulk-dataset. Both use externally snapshotted custody, but each manifest declares its own refresh mechanism, schedule, verifier and rights. Their common service is represented by the shared domain, not a shared lifecycle.
Four units under units/artifacts/<domain>/<collection-slug>, one per event class. Each owns one generated collection and declares its distinct trigger, producer, inputs and clean-build verifier.

Inside the coherent consuming UI unit, place byte-preserved files in vendor/<supplier>/ and freely written styling in src/styles/. Separate custody and rights path rules protect the vendor bytes without inventing a second semantic unit; split the vendor material into its own unit only if it gains independent consumers or refresh ownership.

Separate units at units/tooling/developer/interactive-commands, units/tooling/repository/commit-guards and units/tooling/automation/scheduled-jobs. Extract a libraries/tooling/shared-core unit only for genuinely consumer-neutral code; the three rhythms and failure surfaces remain independent.
units/data/<domain>/<reference-data>, using curated custody and a path-complete rights record for its distinct content licence. Code that reads it uses a reads-data-from edge rather than copying it.

units/assets/brand/trademarks, with restricted redistribution, trademark-specific attribution and copyPolicy fields. Consumers reference or package the asset through declared exports; fingerprint checks catch unrecorded byte copies.

units/studies/<study>/evidence, with delivery.form set to non-shipping and qualityProfile set to the product-code profile. Its realm communicates purpose while its independent assurance field preserves strong gates.

One or more units under units/operations/<system>/<task>, with liveSystemAccess enabled and an operations quality profile covering authentication, dry runs, audit logging, reversibility and human approval. Product gates do not apply unless explicitly selected.

Two units under units/apps/<domain>/<product-app> and units/apps/<domain>/<demo-app>. Their manifests differ in audience and support promise. Near-identical reusable structure moves into a libraries/<domain>/<shared-capability> unit or a generation template rather than being copied.

Extract to units/libraries/datastore/<generic-capability> with datastore-neutral exports and tests. The product-specific pipeline depends on it; the derived graph forbids the generic library from importing the product unit.

Source lives in units/libraries/widgets/<widget>. The serving application lives in units/apps/<domain>/<app>, with built bytes under generated/embedded/<widget-id> and custody naming the widget unit as producer. A generates edge followed by an embeds edge connects source, output and server; CI clean-builds and compares the embedded output.

Two units: units/tooling/repository/commit-hooks and units/tooling/repository/repo-validator. Matching rhythm is outweighed by different consumers and failure contracts. Shared pure logic may live in a small library used by both.

units/libraries/foundation/error-handling. Its tiny size does not disqualify it: the stable contract and extreme derived fan-in justify a narrow, dependency-free unit with especially strict compatibility checks.

units/libraries/security/path-safety, with a security owner, security assurance profile, zero or tightly constrained dependencies and mandatory adversarial tests. Incident origin and criticality are lifecycle metadata, not directory names.

units/libraries/graph/graph-data. Approximately 74 exports do not alone force a split; expose coherent subpath entrypoints and use graph and co-change evidence to decide whether model, traversal, serialization or query capabilities deserve later units. CI applies a public-surface budget and compatibility review.

units/connectors/curriculum/client, with delivery.form set to publicly published, an explicit external package name, service-specific ownership and compatibility policy. Generated types may be a protected subtree or a separate artifact unit according to their rebuild contract.

units/libraries/design/design-tokens, owning curated token sources, compiler code where specific to this contract, and generated/css/. Consumers import the unit's declared CSS export; clean regeneration prevents hand edits to output. A generally reusable compiler would instead be extracted to units/tooling/design/token-compiler.
units/libraries/search/datastore-retrieval, with a commodity-datastore adapter boundary and no product imports. Product-specific ranking policy remains in its consuming product or capability unit.

Decompose the current effective unit into units/data/curriculum/interface-spec-snapshot, units/tooling/curriculum/type-generator, units/artifacts/curriculum/generated-types, units/tooling/curriculum/corpus-miner, units/artifacts/curriculum/mined-corpus, units/data/curriculum/codegen-curation and, only if orchestration has real logic, a thin units/tooling/curriculum/codegen-orchestrator. Typed generates and reads-data-from edges preserve the pipeline, while different refresh, generation, mining and curation lifecycles stop being hidden inside one directory.

units/connectors/observability/<vendor>-adapter. It implements an observability-facing port while containing vendor-specific dependencies and configuration. A vendor-neutral port may live in units/libraries/observability/core if more than one consumer or adapter needs it.

result.design:
A unit is the smallest independently understandable, governable and consumable capability or artefact whose files share one hard contract. Split files when they differ in accountable ownership, edit authority or regeneration mechanism, atomic update trigger, legal exit terms, audience or support promise, assurance profile, portability scope, or independently consumed interface. Keep tests, fixtures and private implementation with their unit when they share its ownership and change lifecycle. Size, file type, co-change frequency and a common external source are not by themselves boundaries. Co-change across units is permitted.

The design answers: what capability these bytes implement; who owns, edits and approves them; whether they are authored, generated, mirrored or byte-preserved; what event changes them and what regenerates them; whether they may be exported freely, under a stated content licence, or not at all; who consumes them and with what support promise; which assurance gates apply; how portable they claim to be; what their public entrypoints are; which typed dependency relationships are allowed; what downstream work a change requires; and the shortest safe route for a newcomer or machine collaborator to inspect and edit them.

The irreducible classifications are seven independent contract dimensions: governance authority; change authority and lifecycle; exit rights; delivery and support contract; assurance and failure profile; portability scope; and API/dependency relations. They remain separate manifest fields rather than being collapsed into labels such as product, tooling or data. A unit's semantic identity and directory are stable locators, not another mutable classification. Whether a unit is a foundation, hub or leaf is derived from the dependency graph rather than encoded in its path.

Layout: substantive files live at /units/<unit-id>/. Each unit has /units/<unit-id>/unit.json and, where applicable, package.json, src/, test/, fixtures/, content/ or payload/. The manifest identifies actual entrypoints, so tools never need to infer them by scanning. The root contains estate.json, a generated units.index.json and the minimum package-manager/build bootstraps. estate.json assigns those exceptional root files to the estate-control unit; every other tracked file must belong to exactly one /units/<unit-id> root. There are no type, domain, team or lifecycle directory tiers. Mutable classifications therefore change without moving files, and doubling the estate adds siblings rather than new roots.

unit.json contains schemaVersion, id, purpose, governance, provenance, change, rights, delivery, assurance, scope, api, dependencies, relations and workflows. governance identifies the accountable human owner, permitted editors and required approvers. provenance records authored, generated, external-snapshot or vendor-preserved authority, the upstream identity, generator unit and byte-preservation requirement. change records the atomic trigger, schedule or event class and regeneration command. rights records SPDX identifiers, notices and exportPolicy as freely-exportable, content-licensed or estate-only. delivery records audience, publication/deployment form, support promise and release payload. assurance names a centrally defined gate profile plus justified additions. scope is portable, estate, domain:<id> or product:<id>. api lists code and artefact entrypoints. dependencies and relations contain typed edges such as runtime, build, test, generates, generated-from, embeds and deploys. workflows supplies readFirst, build, test, regenerate and safe-edit commands.

Names are globally unique, lowercase kebab-case capability nouns. Reusable capabilities use names such as path-safety or graph-data; executable boundary adapters use descriptive suffixes such as -cli, -hook, -job or -adapter; externally sourced artefacts use -snapshot, -dataset or -assets; audience variants use -app and -demo. Names never encode ownership, licence, quality tier or directory layer. TypeScript imports use @estate/<unit-id> and only declared exports; a public package may additionally declare its stable external publication name.

units.index.json is generated from all manifests and contains every id, path, purpose, aliases, entrypoints, owners, classifications, forward edges and reverse edges. Finding a unit costs one predictable file read; understanding how to work on it costs its one manifest read; readFirst then names the minimum source entrypoints. An old id can remain as a catalog alias during a deprecation window.

A graph validator resolves actual imports and artefact flows, compares them with declared edges and rejects cross-unit relative imports, undeclared edges and non-exported entrypoint access. Portable units may not depend on narrower estate, domain or product scopes; estate units may not depend on product-specific units unless explicitly acting as a boundary adapter. Production release closures may not include demo, research, live-operations or estate-only artefacts. Public release closures must have compatible rights and generate required notices. Cycles are rejected except for an explicitly modelled, reviewed test-only cycle.

For a change, tooling maps changed files to units, computes reverse dependency and relation closures, reports affected owners and consumers, checks generated-output input digests, runs each affected unit's declared gates and runs consumer contract checks when an exported interface changes. A stale generated artefact, invalid legal closure, missing required approval, untested affected contract or catalog drift is a hard failure. Fast structural, import and provenance checks run at commit time; complete affected-graph, release-rights and assurance checks run in CI; drift checks for external snapshots may run on their declared schedules.

Machine-enforced rules are manifest schema and completeness, unique ids, file ownership coverage, catalog freshness, naming syntax, import/export boundaries, dependency directions and cycles, generated provenance/digests, byte-preservation hashes, release-rights closure, required notices, affected-unit gate execution and review approval mapping. Human judgment remains necessary for whether a purpose is coherent, whether two capabilities should share an identity, whether declared ownership/support/licensing is truthful and whether a split or merge improves comprehension. Exceptions live only in estate.json with an owner, reason and expiry and are rejected after expiry.

Splitting a unit means creating new manifests, moving the relevant files, declaring edges, mechanically rewriting package imports and retaining aliases where compatibility requires them. Merging reverses that operation after confirming all seven contracts agree and no independent public consumer remains. Neither operation changes unrelated paths. Manifest classifications can be corrected without a move; schema changes use schemaVersion plus an automated manifest migration. This keeps organisational correction cheaper than a directory-taxonomy re-root.

organisingRules.name: Unit identity and boundary
organisingRules.rule: Give a capability or artefact its own unit when it has an independent public interface or any hard contract dimension differs; do not split merely for size, file kind or frequent co-change.
organisingRules.carrier: One stable directory /units/<unit-id>, one unit.json manifest and exhaustive file-ownership validation.

organisingRules.name: Semantic naming
organisingRules.rule: Use globally unique lowercase kebab-case capability names; suffix only concrete boundary forms such as -app, -demo, -cli, -hook, -job, -adapter, -snapshot, -dataset or -assets. Do not encode mutable governance or taxonomy in paths.
organisingRules.carrier: Directory name, unit.json id, @estate/<unit-id> import name and generated catalog aliases.

organisingRules.name: Governance authority
organisingRules.rule: Every byte has one accountable human owner, a permitted editor policy and explicit approval requirements. Differing governance is a unit boundary.
organisingRules.carrier: unit.json governance fields, generated review-ownership configuration and protected-branch approval enforcement.

organisingRules.name: Change authority and lifecycle
organisingRules.rule: State whether bytes are authored, generated, externally snapshotted or vendor-preserved, together with their atomic trigger and regeneration authority. Differing triggers or mechanisms require separate artefact units even when the upstream source is shared.
organisingRules.carrier: unit.json provenance and change fields; generator relations, input digests, byte hashes and stale-output checks.

organisingRules.name: Exit rights
organisingRules.rule: Classify each unit as freely exportable, content-licensed or estate-only and record exact licences and notices. A release is allowed only when the complete dependency and embedded-artefact closure is compatible.
organisingRules.carrier: unit.json rights and delivery payload fields plus graph-based release-closure and notice-generation checks.

organisingRules.name: Delivery and support contract
organisingRules.rule: Declare audience, publication or deployment form and support promise independently of code quality. Production, demo, research, operations, public-package and embedded-artefact contracts are not interchangeable.
organisingRules.carrier: unit.json delivery fields and deployment/publication policy checks.

organisingRules.name: Assurance and failure profile
organisingRules.rule: Assign gates according to consequence and failure mode rather than directory. Security, evidence, operations, product, generated-integrity and byte-integrity profiles may differ from delivery classification.
organisingRules.carrier: unit.json assurance profile and centrally versioned executable gate definitions enforced for affected units.

organisingRules.name: Portability scope
organisingRules.rule: Declare whether a capability is portable, estate-wide, domain-specific or product-specific. Dependencies may point from narrower scope to broader scope, not the reverse, except through an explicit boundary adapter.
organisingRules.carrier: unit.json scope field and graph-based dependency-direction checks.

organisingRules.name: API and dependency relations
organisingRules.rule: All cross-unit use goes through declared code or artefact entrypoints and a typed relation. Relative imports across unit roots and undeclared consumers are forbidden.
organisingRules.carrier: unit.json api, dependencies and relations fields, package exports and comparison with the resolved TypeScript/build graph.

organisingRules.name: Navigation cost
organisingRules.rule: A collaborator must be able to locate any unit without scanning directories and learn the safe first reads and commands from one local manifest.
organisingRules.carrier: Generated root units.index.json plus unit.json purpose, readFirst and workflow fields.

organisingRules.name: Change impact
organisingRules.rule: Every changed file maps to a unit; reverse graph traversal identifies consumers, required regenerations, contract tests, owners and incompatible release closures.
organisingRules.carrier: Dependency graph derived from resolved imports and declared generates, embeds, deploys, build, test and runtime edges.

organisingRules.name: Evolution
organisingRules.rule: Keep classification out of directory tiers, permit multi-unit commits and make splits, merges and corrections mechanical. Temporary deviations must be owned and expire.
organisingRules.carrier: Flat unit root, versioned manifests, catalog aliases, import codemods and expiring exceptions in estate.json.

probePlacements.placement: Place the interface snapshot in /units/external-service-interface-snapshot and the bulk data in /units/external-service-bulk-dataset. Each is an external-snapshot artefact with its own change trigger, digest and generated-from edge; distinct refresh implementations are separate -refresh tool units. Sharing an upstream service creates catalog metadata, not containment.

Create four sibling generated artefact units, one per event class, each with its own generator relation, trigger and freshness digest. Extract a shared generator library only for genuinely event-neutral machinery.

Put byte-preserved files in /units/<vendor>-vendor-files with vendor-preserved provenance, hash enforcement and no human edit workflow. Put the authored styling in /units/<surface>-styles with ordinary code ownership and gates.

Use /units/<tooling>-cli, /units/<tooling>-commit-guard and /units/<tooling>-scheduled-job for the three consumer and lifecycle contracts. Place only neutral reusable implementation in /units/<tooling>-shared-machinery, and omit that fourth unit if no true shared capability exists.

Place it in /units/<subject>-reference-data with authored-curated provenance, content-licensed exportPolicy, exact licence and notice metadata, and artefact entrypoints. Code consumers depend on it rather than housing it.
Place the images in /units/brand-trademark-assets with restricted rights, approved-audience delivery rules and explicit embed edges. Release-closure validation blocks unapproved reuse.
Place it in /units/<study>-evidence with delivery set to research-nonshipping and assurance set to the product-quality or evidence profile. Nonshipping status does not weaken its gates.

Place each coherent live-system capability in /units/live-operations-<task>, with estate-only delivery and an operations assurance profile containing permissions, dry-run, audit and approval controls instead of product gates.

Use /units/<product>-app for the supported deployment and /units/<product>-demo for the demonstration. They may depend on shared capability units, but structural similarity does not merge their audiences, release paths or support promises.

Extract the generic code to /units/datastore-pipeline-machinery with portable scope and a datastore-neutral API. The product-specific pipeline remains a narrower unit that depends on it; the graph check prevents the portable unit depending back on product code.

Keep source in /units/<widget>, built bytes in /units/<widget>-embed as a generated artefact unit, and the serving application in /units/<host>-app. Model source-to-output with generates/generated-from and output-to-host with embeds; deployment materialises the artefact rather than treating copied bytes as authored host source.

Use /units/commit-hook-guard and /units/repo-state-validator. Their common cadence does not outweigh distinct consumers, failure modes and assurance contracts. Share a third neutral library only if actual implementation is independently coherent.

Place it in /units/error-result as a portable, zero-dependency library with a deliberately tiny export surface. Its high reverse-dependency reach is derived from the graph and causes broad compatibility checks without changing its path.

Place it in /units/path-safety with portable scope, security assurance, security-owner approval and focused adversarial tests. Small size does not justify hiding a security boundary inside generic utilities.

Place it in /units/graph-data. Keep one unit while its approximately 74 symbols share ownership, lifecycle and capability; organise supported sub-entrypoints through package exports and split only when an independently consumed contract emerges.

Place it in /units/curriculum-client with domain:curriculum scope, public-package delivery, a declared external package name, open-code rights, semantic-version and API compatibility gates, and only export-compatible dependencies.

Place authored transformation code in /units/design-token-pipeline and generated CSS in /units/design-tokens-css. Connect them with generates/generated-from relations; consuming surfaces depend on the CSS artefact entrypoint and freshness checks detect stale output.

Place it in /units/datastore-search with portable scope, a commodity-datastore-facing API and no product dependencies. Product-specific ranking, curriculum semantics or deployment adapters remain in narrower consumers.

Decompose it into /units/curriculum-spec-refresh, /units/curriculum-spec-snapshot, /units/curriculum-type-generator, /units/curriculum-generated-types, /units/curriculum-corpus-miner, /units/curriculum-mined-corpus and /units/curriculum-curated-overlays. Add /units/curriculum-codegen-orchestrator only for thin authored orchestration. Typed generator edges preserve the pipeline while separating external snapshots, authored tools, generated artefacts and curated content.

Place it in /units/<vendor>-observability-adapter with portable or estate scope according to its imports, isolate the vendor dependency there and expose the estate's observability contract through explicit exports. A vendor-neutral observability API becomes a separate unit only if independently consumed.

result.design:
## Monorepo Organizational Design

### Questions This Design Answers

1. **What makes two things separate units?** They differ along one of: delivery/deployment boundary, publication model, quality-gate membership, target audience, generation mode, or consumer interface. These boundaries determine governance rules, CI/CD flows, and dependency constraints.

2. **Where do units live?** By delivery tier expressed in directory structure (apps/ → products; packages/ → libraries; agent-tools/ → operational infrastructure; demos/ → references; research/ → evidence). All other organizational characteristics are expressed in machine-readable metadata.

3. **How are they named?** Via @oaknational/[category]-[unit-name] convention in package.json name field, where category signals domain (curriculum, design, graph, etc.) and unit-name identifies the component.

4. **How are rules enforced?** Via: eslint-plugin-standards boundary rules; dependency-cruiser configuration; turbo.json task graph and input/output specifications; husky hooks; and custom validators in agent-tools repo-check suite.

### Minimal Independent Classifications (8 core dimensions)

All classified in `estate` metadata field in package.json except delivery-tier (directory-expressed):

1. **Delivery Tier** (directory-only) — Where in pipeline: apps | packages | agent-tools | demos | research

2. **Publication Model** — Public npm | workspace-private | internal-only

3. **Quality Gate Membership** — Full gates (build/type-check/lint/test) | partial gates | research-gated | unshipped

4. **Content Licenses** — Array of: MIT | OGL | Trademark | Design | Vendor

5. **Generation Mode** — Hand-written | generated | artifact-collection | configuration-driven | multi-stage

6. **Refresh Cadence** — On-demand | event-driven | scheduled | continuous | one-time

7. **Consumer Interface** — npm-import | cli-command | embedded-build | filesystem | api-endpoint

8. **Audience/Support Promise** — public-sdk | internal-product | internal-tooling | reference-demo | research-study

### Organising Rules (carrying each classification)

**RULE 1: Delivery Tier** (Directory)
- Carrier: Exact directory depth
- Enforcement: depcruise and eslint-plugin-standards cross-boundary rules
- apps/* → exported, production-deployable
- packages/core/* → shared infrastructure, zero external-service deps
- packages/libs/* → reusable domain libraries
- packages/sdks/* → public and internal client interfaces
- packages/design/* → design system and visual assets
- agent-tools/* → operational tooling, runs against live systems
- demos/* → reference implementations, no user SLA
- research/* → quality-gated evidence code, never shipped
- Property: `estate.deliveryTier` (derived from path, not manifest-stored)

**RULE 2: Publication Model** (Manifest field)
- Carrier: package.json `publishConfig.access` (restricted|open) and `private` (true|false)
- Enforcement: CI pipeline publish step validates against manifest
- Property: `estate.publicationModel` = "public" | "workspace-restricted" | "internal-only"

**RULE 3: Quality Gate Membership** (Manifest + Enforcement)
- Carrier: `estate.qualityGates` array in package.json
- Enforcement: turbo.json task dependencies and agent-tools repo-check
- Arrays of: build | type-check | lint | test | test:e2e | test:ui | test:a11y | mutate | publish
- Research units use own internal turbo, gated by research-evidence membership

**RULE 4: Content Licenses** (Manifest field)
- Carrier: `estate.contentLicenses` array
- Enforcement: header-check scripts and license-audit validators
- Permitted: ["MIT"], ["OGL"], ["Trademark"], ["Design"], ["Vendor"], or combinations

**RULE 5: Generation Mode** (Manifest field)
- Carrier: `estate.generationMode` string
- Enforcement: turbo.json sdk-codegen task, scripts validation
- Values: hand-written | generated (from OpenAPI, schemas) | artifact-collection (external fetch) | configuration-driven (build-time) | multi-stage (sequence of above)
- Generated code: marked read-only, inputs tracked as turbo cache keys

**RULE 6: Refresh Cadence** (Manifest field)
- Carrier: `estate.refreshCadence` string and optional `estate.refreshTriggers` array
- Enforcement: agent-tools validate-stale-script-invocations, schedule documentation
- Values: on-demand | event-driven (list: sdk-codegen-run, design-system-change, ...) | scheduled (cron) | continuous | one-time

**RULE 7: Consumer Interface** (Manifest field)
- Carrier: `estate.consumerInterfaces` array
- Enforcement: dependency-cruiser consumption rules per interface type
- Values: npm-import | cli-command | cli-hook | embedded-build | filesystem | api-endpoint | mcp-tool
- Determines whether unit is accessed at build-time, dev-time, runtime, or deployment-time

**RULE 8: Audience & Support Promise** (Manifest field)
- Carrier: `estate.audience` string and `estate.supportPromise` string
- Enforcement: Sonar quality gate strictness, version bump policy, deprecation timeline
- Audience values: public-sdk | internal-product | internal-tooling | reference-demo | research-study
- Support promise: (if public-sdk) pin major version + SemVer, (if demo) "reference-only", (if research) "not-shipped"

### Layout This Design Implies

```
oak-open-curriculum-ecosystem/
├── apps/
│   ├── oak-curriculum-mcp-streamable-http/   (delivery-tier: apps)
│   │   ├── widget/                           (embedded-build consumer)
│   │   └── src/
│   │       ├── mcp-tools/                    (P4: tooling for multiple rhythms)
│   │       ├── landing-page/                 (baked at build time)
│   │       └── server.ts
│   └── [other-products]/
│
├── packages/
│   ├── core/                                  (shared infrastructure, leaf/near-leaf)
│   │   ├── result/                           (S1: error primitive, widely imported)
│   │   ├── safe-path/                        (S2: security-critical utility)
│   │   ├── graph-core/                       (S3: large graph library, ~74 symbols)
│   │   ├── type-helpers/
│   │   ├── env/
│   │   └── workspace-config/
│   │
│   ├── libs/                                  (reusable domain libraries)
│   │   ├── graph-ingest/                     (ingestion modes, source mapping)
│   │   ├── search-contracts/                 (P4 probe: consumed by multiple surfaces)
│   │   ├── logger/
│   │   ├── posthog-node/                     (S8: observability adapter)
│   │   ├── sentry-node/                      (S8: observability adapter)

│   │   ├── oak-curriculum-sdk/               (S4: typed client, published public)

│       ├── oak-design-system/                (P3: vendor files + styling)
│       ├── oak-design-tokens/                (S5: design-token pipeline → CSS)

│   │   ├── docs/

│   └── [other studies]
│
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml                       (workspace members)

└── [repo governance]
```

### Probe Placements

**Product/Feature Probes:**

**P1:** Interface snapshot (API schema) + bulk dataset (refreshed separately)
- Placement: **packages/sdks/oak-sdk-codegen**
- Classifications: generation=artifact-collection, refreshCadence=event-driven (schema fetch ≠ bulk data triggers), consumerInterface=npm-import
- Carrier: estate.generation, estate.refreshCadence, estate.refreshTriggers
- ForcedFit: false

**P2:** Four machine-regenerated artifact collections, different event triggers
- Placement: **agent-tools/src/corpus-analysis** + **packages/sdks/oak-sdk-codegen/generated/** outputs
- Classifications: generation=artifact-collection, refreshCadence=event-driven, multiple distinct trigger events
- Carrier: estate.refreshTriggers (array per artifact), turbo.json env blocks for trigger variables
- ForcedFit: false

**P3:** Vendor files (byte-preserved) + hand-written styling
- Placement: **packages/design/oak-design-system** (vendor files) + **packages/design/oak-design-system/components.css** (styling)
- Classifications: contentLicenses=["Vendor", "MIT"], generationMode=hand-written (for styling), mutation-policy=immutable-vendor
- Carrier: estate.contentLicenses (array), eslint-plugin-standards immutability rules via file path
- ForcedFit: false

**P4:** Tooling area serving multiple consumers on different rhythms
- Placement: **agent-tools/** (root)
- Classifications: consumerInterfaces=["cli-commit-hook", "cli-scheduled-job", "cli-interactive"], qualityGates=["build", "type-check", "lint", "test"]
- Carrier: estate.consumerInterfaces (array), turbo.json tasks for each consumer rhythm
- ForcedFit: false

organisingRules.name: Delivery Tier Boundary
organisingRules.rule: Units are segregated by deployment context into five tiers, expressed by directory depth: apps/ (products), packages/ (libraries), agent-tools/ (operational), demos/ (references), research/ (evidence). Cross-tier dependencies must satisfy direction constraints: apps→packages,libs,sdks,core; packages→packages/core,libs; agent-tools→packages; demos→packages; research→packages. Violation caught by depcruise and eslint-plugin-standards.

organisingRules.name: Publication Model
organisingRules.rule: A unit is public (open npm), workspace-restricted (npm with limited access), or internal-only (workspace member, never published). Declared in package.json via `private: true/false` and `publishConfig.access`. Automated by CI: public units receive full publish workflow, workspace-restricted get npm push with scope restriction, internal-only skip publish entirely.

organisingRules.rule: Each unit declares which gates apply via estate.qualityGates array: build, type-check, lint, test, test:e2e, test:ui, test:a11y, mutate, publish. Research units gate their own code but never ship. Product apps gate everything. Libraries gate build/type-check/lint/test; optional: mutate. Enforcement: turbo.json task dependencies; repo-check validation.
organisingRules.carrier: package.json: estate.qualityGates (array of gate names)

organisingRules.name: Content License Segregation
organisingRules.rule: Each unit declares content licenses via estate.contentLicenses array. Permitted: MIT (code), OGL (open curriculum), Trademark (brand assets), Design (design system), Vendor (immutable third-party). organisingRules.carrier: package.json: estate.contentLicenses (array)

organisingRules.name: Generation Mode Classification
organisingRules.rule: Units are classified by how content is created: hand-written (human authored), generated (from spec/schema), artifact-collection (external fetch), configuration-driven (build-time transformation), or multi-stage (sequence). Generated code is read-only; inputs tracked as turbo cache keys. Enforcement: turbo.json input globs; eslint no-manual-edit rules on generated paths.
organisingRules.carrier: package.json: estate.generationMode (enum)

organisingRules.name: Refresh Cadence & Triggers
organisingRules.rule: Units declare refresh schedule via estate.refreshCadence (on-demand | event-driven | scheduled | continuous | one-time) and estate.refreshTriggers (array of event names for event-driven). Event triggers are: sdk-codegen-run, design-system-change, curriculum-api-schema-change, etc. Enforcement: agent-tools validate-stale-script-invocations checks invocation times match cadence.
organisingRules.carrier: package.json: estate.refreshCadence (enum) + estate.refreshTriggers (array)

organisingRules.name: Consumer Interface Routing
organisingRules.rule: Units declare how they are consumed via estate.consumerInterfaces (array of: npm-import | cli-command | cli-hook | embedded-build | filesystem | api-endpoint | mcp-tool). Determines access-time (build vs dev vs runtime), impact scope (whole tree vs local to consumer), and dependency rules. Enforcement: dependency-cruiser rules per interface type; turbo.json cache keys.
organisingRules.carrier: package.json: estate.consumerInterfaces (array of interface types)

organisingRules.name: Audience & Support Promise
organisingRules.rule: Each unit declares audience (public-sdk | internal-product | internal-tooling | reference-demo | research-study) and support promise (semver+deprecation, production-sla, reference-only, not-shipped, etc.). Public SDKs follow SemVer, maintain deprecation timelines, and pin majors. Internal tools don't. Research never ships. Demos have no SLA. Enforcement: version-bump validation; CI publish gating.
organisingRules.carrier: package.json: estate.audience + estate.supportPromise (enums)

**Questions This Task Statement Should Have Asked But Did Not:**

1. **How should units declare their dependencies on external services?** The design assumes `estate.externalService` and `estate.externalVendor` metadata, but the task didn't specify whether this should be machine-readable or inferred from package.json dependencies. Answer: Recommend explicit metadata field with version floor documentation.

2. **What enforcement mechanism should prevent accidental scope leakage?** When a generic/reusable unit (S1, S2, S3) becomes domain-specific or vice versa, how is that boundary breach detected? Answer: depcruise rules keyed on estate.scope + estatelevel boundary rules.

3. **How should the design express "this unit must not be split further" vs "this unit is a candidate for extraction"?** P10 is naturally a forced fit because generic machinery is embedded in a product-specific pipeline. Should there be an explicit `extractionCandidate` or `atomicUnit` flag? Answer: Yes, `estate.extractionStatus` field for coordination.

4. **What's the versioning policy for multi-stage generated code (S7)?** When oak-sdk-codegen produces types, schemas, MCP descriptors, and bulk data with different change frequencies, how are version bumps coordinated? Answer: Estate metadata should specify per-output-format version strategies.

5. **How should the design represent consumed-but-not-produced outputs?** The MCP app embeds widget HTML that's produced by a Vite build. Is the widget itself a separate unit or just a build artifact of the app? Answer: Recommend separate if it has its own quality gates or refreshes independently.

6. **Should there be an explicit "compatibility tier" classification for how freely units can change?** Currently private (internal) units have more freedom than public SDKs, but should there be intermediate tiers (e.g., "internal-stable" vs "internal-experimental")? Answer: Could extend supportPromise field with stability markers.

7. **How does the design handle units with asymmetric quality requirements?** An operational script might need full security review but no mutation testing, while a library might need mutation but not security review. Is the gate array sufficient or should gate membership be tupled with strictness? Answer: Current array model is sufficient; individual gates can have optional strictness modifiers if needed.

8. **Should there be explicit metadata for "this unit is part of a release bundle"?** The SDK codegen produces multiple outputs consumed together; should they be marked as a logical release unit? Answer: Yes, `estate.releaseUnit` field pointing to a coordinated group would improve publish automation.

result.design:
**Distribution Tier (Single Directory Classification)**
- `packages/` = shipped to npm users; public API contracts; full quality gates; may only depend on other packages or stdlib
- `internal/` = monorepo-only infrastructure; no publishing; can depend on either tier

**Six Independent Metadata Classifications (expressed in package.json + build/CI config):**

1. **License Class** (`license` field): MIT | OGL | RESERVED
   - Enforced by: CI license scanner, build system prevents mixing in output
   - Dependency rule: OGL-licensed packages can only import other OGL or MIT; reserved assets isolated to reserved packages

2. **Update Mechanism** (`refreshPattern` field with driver, frequency, trigger, url, mechanism)
   - Drivers: spec-fetch | bulk-fetch | hand-curated | generated | vendor-supplied | static
   - Enforced by: CI job routing, separate versioning per pattern, independent lock files

3. **Content Authority** (`changeability` field): hand-written | generated | byte-preserved
   - Enforced by: naming conventions (*.gen.ts, *.vendor.js), pre-commit hooks that reject edits, linting rules

4. **Quality Gate Level** (`qualityGates` field): full | research | build | none
   - Full: test suite + type checks + linting + code review (all shipped code)
   - Research: type checks + linting (internal research, no production tests)
   - Build: compilation only (build infrastructure, ops tools)
   - None: reserved for operational scripts run against live systems
   - Enforced by: CI check routing based on gate level

5. **Artifact Consumption** (`builtOutput` field with outputDir, embedIn, serveAt, consumed)
   - Routing: copy to declared directory, embed in specified packages, serve at path, or internal-only
   - Enforced by: build system only outputs to declared locations; embedIn triggers build-time node_modules injection

6. **Reusability Scope** (`scope` field): generic | product-specific
   - Generic: reusable across similar datastores or domains (no Oak-specifics)
   - Product-specific: coupled to Oak infrastructure or pedagogy
   - Enforced by: semantic versioning (scope change = major bump), documentation and dependency review

**Enforcement Mechanisms:**
- Dependency direction: CI audits dependency graph; packages/* cannot import internal/*; internal/* may import both
- License mixing: CI scanner prevents shipped unit depending on OGL unless self-is-OGL; prevents OGL→reserved dependencies
- Generation/vendor integrity: Pre-commit hook fails if *.gen.* or *.vendor.* files are modified (must regenerate or vendor-update)
- Quality gate compliance: CI gates routed per package's declared level; failures at wrong gate are caught at merge time
- Built output isolation: Build system respects builtOutput declaration; artifacts placed only to declared targets
- Generic machinery: S3 graph library and S1/S2 stdlib are imported only; larger reusable units document their generic boundaries

**Probe Case Placement:**

P1 (External service snapshot + bulk data, different schedules):
- **Placement**: `packages/curriculum/types/` (spec snapshot) + `packages/curriculum/corpus/` (bulk data) — two separate packages
- **Metadata**: @oak/curriculum-types { refreshPattern: {driver: "spec-fetch", frequency: "29/year"}, changeability: "generated" }; @oak/curriculum-corpus { refreshPattern: {driver: "bulk-fetch", frequency: "7/year"}, changeability: "generated" }
- **ForcedFit: true** — Design assumes one package per distinct refresh pattern, but probe presents them as one unit; recommendation is to split into two packages for independent versioning and CI routing

P2 (Four machine-regenerated artifact collections, different event triggers):
- **Placement**: `internal/build/generated/` as separate @internal packages per trigger, OR one package with four sub-components
- **Metadata**: refreshPattern: {driver: "generated", trigger: "spec-change|corpus-update|design-token-export|search-index"}, changeability: "generated", qualityGates: "build"
- **ForcedFit: false** — Design handles via refreshPattern field and build graph tagging; could be one package or four

P3 (Vendor files + hand-written styling, byte-preserved vs. editable):
- **Placement**: `packages/ui/design-system/`
- **Metadata**: license: "MIT", qualityGates: "full"; sub-tree organization: `vendor/` (vendor files with .vendor. naming), `src/` (hand-written)
- **Enforcement**: Linting rules treat .vendor.* files as byte-preserved; hand-written CSS in src/ is edited normally; pre-commit hook prevents vendor/ edits
- **ForcedFit: false** — Design handles via naming conventions and directory sub-structure; no hard enforcement at manifest level needed

P4 (Tooling with multiple consumers on different rhythms):
- **Placement**: `internal/tooling/` as @internal/build-tools or split per consumer (@internal/commit-guards, @internal/cli-tools, @internal/scheduled-jobs)
- **Metadata**: consumers: ["commit-hooks", "build-system", "scheduled-jobs", "interactive-cli"]
- **ForcedFit: false** — Design handles via consumers field in metadata; larger repos might split into separate packages for clearer dependency direction

P5 (Hand-curated reference data, different license):
- **Placement**: `packages/curriculum/reference/` as separate @oak/curriculum-reference package
- **Metadata**: license: "OGL", changeability: "hand-written", qualityGates: "full", scope: "product-specific"
- **Enforcement**: CI license scanner ensures OGL package only appears in OGL-licensed build outputs or products
- **ForcedFit: false**

P6 (Trademark images, reserved license terms):
- **Placement**: `packages/ui/brand-assets/` or `packages/brand/`
- **Metadata**: license: "RESERVED", changeability: "hand-written", qualityGates: "full"; filename pattern: trademark-*.svg, brand-*.svg
- **Enforcement**: License scanner isolates reserved assets; CI prevents their inclusion in public-distribution artifacts unless explicitly approved
- **ForcedFit: false**

P7 (Research code, quality-gated but not shipped):
- **Placement**: `internal/research/`
- **Metadata**: qualityGates: "research", consumers: ["internal-research"], packageType: "internal"
- **Enforcement**: CI routes research-level checks (type + lint, no production tests)
- **ForcedFit: false**

P8 (Operational scripts outside product gates):
- **Placement**: `internal/ops/scripts/`
- **Metadata**: qualityGates: "none", consumers: ["live-systems"], packageType: "internal", changeability: "hand-written"
- **Note**: No automated checks; approval via manual review/change log in separate operational registry
- **ForcedFit: false**

P9 (Product app + demo app, near-identical structure, different audiences):
- **Placement**: Both in `packages/ui/` if both shipped, OR product in `packages/ui/mcp-server/`, demo in `internal/demos/` if demo is internal-only
- **Metadata**: @oak/mcp-server { consumers: ["end-users"], qualityGates: "full" } vs @oak/demo-apps { consumers: ["developers"], qualityGates: "full" } [or research if internal]
- **Enforcement**: Consumers field documents audience; if demo is shipped as @oak/demo-apps, it carries same quality gates as product but different semantic versioning (demo@0.x, product@1.x or vice versa)
- **ForcedFit: false**

P10 (Generic machinery embedded in product-specific pipeline):
- **Placement**: `packages/stdlib/graph/` (generic, S3) consumed by `packages/curriculum/codegen/` (product-specific, S7)
- **Metadata**: @oak/stdlib-graph { scope: "generic" }; @oak/curriculum-codegen { scope: "product-specific" }
- **Enforcement**: Dependency graph makes direction explicit; CI could flag if generic machinery re-imports product-specific code
- **ForcedFit: false**

P11 (Browser widget source + embedded built output):
- **Placement**: Source in `packages/ui/widget/`, built output copied to `packages/ui/mcp-server/dist/` via build system
- **Metadata**: @oak/widget { builtOutput: {outputDir: "dist/", embedIn: ["@oak/mcp"], consumed: "embedded-artifact"} }
- **Enforcement**: Build system uses embedIn field to inject built artifacts into consumer node_modules; versioning independent
- **ForcedFit: false**

P12 (Commit-hook guards + repo validators, same rhythm, different consumers/failure modes):
- **Placement**: Both in `internal/tooling/` as @internal/repo-guards or split: @internal/commit-guards, @internal/repo-validators
- **Metadata**: changeability: "hand-written", qualityGates: "build"; consumers: ["commit-hooks", "ci-system"] with separate entry points
- **Enforcement**: Pre-commit hook routes to commit-guard exit code; CI system routes to validator exit code; different failure handling
- **ForcedFit: false** — Design handles via consumers field; could be one package with multiple entry points or two separate packages

**Small/Reusable Libraries:**

S1 (Error-handling primitive, zero deps): `packages/stdlib/errors/` — {scope: "generic", qualityGates: "full"}
S2 (Path-safety utility, security-critical): `packages/stdlib/path-safety/` — {scope: "generic", qualityGates: "full", securityCritical: true [optional field for enforcement]}
S3 (Large graph library, 74 symbols): `packages/stdlib/graph/` — {scope: "generic", qualityGates: "full"}
S4 (Typed curriculum client): `packages/curriculum/client/` — {scope: "product-specific", qualityGates: "full"}
S5 (Design-token pipeline): `packages/ui/design-system/tokens/` — {refreshPattern: {driver: "hand-curated"|"generated", trigger: "..."}, builtOutput: {outputDir: "dist/", consumed: "css+js+json"}, qualityGates: "full"}
S6 (Search-retrieval library): `packages/search/retrieval/` — {scope: "product-specific", qualityGates: "full"}
S7 (Largest unit, spec + codegen + corpus): `packages/curriculum/codegen/` — **ForcedFit: true** — This package has multiple sub-components with different refreshPattern drivers (spec-fetch, generated, bulk-fetch, hand-curated) under one package.json. Design should extend to allow "subcomponents" field listing each component's refreshPattern separately, OR split into @oak/curriculum-spec, @oak/curriculum-corpus, @oak/curriculum-codegen
S8 (Observability adapter): `packages/infra/observability/` — {scope: "generic", qualityGates: "full"}

organisingRules.name: Distribution Tier Gates API Contracts and Dependencies
organisingRules.rule: Code in packages/ is published to npm and establishes public API contracts; passes full quality gates; can only depend on other packages/* or stdlib. Code in internal/ stays in monorepo; never published; may depend on either tier. CI audits dependency direction at every commit.
organisingRules.carrier: Directory structure (packages/ vs internal/), package.json packageType field, CI dependency audit, npm publishing rules

organisingRules.name: License Class Prevents Mixing
organisingRules.rule: Each shipped package has a single license class (MIT, OGL, or RESERVED). OGL-licensed packages can depend on other OGL or MIT; MIT can depend on MIT but not OGL; RESERVED is isolated to reserved-only packages. Build outputs cannot mix license classes.
organisingRules.carrier: package.json license field, CI license scanner, build system validation, dependency resolver

organisingRules.name: Update Mechanism Routes CI and Controls Versioning
organisingRules.rule: refreshPattern field specifies driver (spec-fetch, bulk-fetch, hand-curated, generated, vendor-supplied, static), frequency, and trigger. Spec-fetch packages version independently of bulk-fetch packages; each gets separate lock file and regeneration schedule. Generated artifacts are regenerated and verified before commit; vendor files are treated as byte-preserved.
organisingRules.carrier: package.json refreshPattern field, build graph tags, CI job routing, separate lock files per pattern, pre-commit hooks

organisingRules.name: Content Authority Enforces Editing Boundaries
organisingRules.rule: hand-written files can be edited freely; generated files (*.gen.*) and vendor files (*.vendor.*) fail linting if modified and must be regenerated or vendor-updated before commit. Pre-commit hook enforces this; linting fails any manual edits to byte-preserved files.
organisingRules.carrier: package.json changeability field, file naming conventions, pre-commit hooks, linting rules

organisingRules.name: Quality Gate Level Routes Test and Check Requirements
organisingRules.rule: full gates = test suite + type checks + linting + code review (all shipped code); research gates = type checks + linting only (internal research); build gates = compilation only (infrastructure, build tools); none gates = manual review only (ops scripts on live systems). CI routes checks based on declared level.
organisingRules.carrier: package.json qualityGates field, CI check routing configuration, stage-gated test suites

organisingRules.name: Built Output Routing Isolates Artifacts
organisingRules.rule: builtOutput field declares where built artifacts go: outputDir specifies directory in package, embedIn lists packages that receive injected artifacts at build time, serveAt specifies live-serve path. Build system outputs only to declared locations; consumers pull from those locations only.
organisingRules.carrier: package.json builtOutput field with outputDir, embedIn, serveAt, consumed properties; build system configuration

organisingRules.name: Reusability Scope Constrains Usage Context
organisingRules.rule: generic machinery (S1, S2, S3, S6) works against any similar datastore; product-specific (S4, S5, S7, S8) assumes Oak infrastructure or pedagogy. Scope change is a major version bump. Dependency graph should reflect no reverse-imports (product-specific cannot import generic as generic would become product-specific).
organisingRules.carrier: package.json scope field, semantic versioning discipline, dependency graph structure, documentation

organisingRules.name: Multi-Pattern Packages Require Sub-Component Tracking
organisingRules.rule: When one package contains multiple distinct refresh drivers (e.g., spec-fetch AND bulk-fetch AND hand-curated AND generated), declare them via subcomponents field listing each component's refreshPattern separately, OR split into separate packages per driver. This enables correct CI routing and independent versioning.
organisingRules.carrier: package.json subcomponents field (optional/recommended), OR split into separate packages; build graph tagging per sub-component

organisingRules.name: Generic Machinery Does Not Import Product-Specific Code
organisingRules.rule: @oak/stdlib/* and other generic packages export only reusable abstractions; they never depend on product-specific units. This ensures generality can be extracted and reused. CI detects and rejects reverse-imports (generic←product).
organisingRules.carrier: Dependency graph analysis, CI checks, linting configuration
