fixDesign.design:
PRINCIPLE: four facts organise the estate; each lives in the cheapest carrier that can hold it truthfully, and every declared fact has a CI check that RECOMPUTES it rather than trusting the declaration. Fact 1 — LICENCE (immutable per unit) is carried by a root partition. Fact 2 — AUDIENCE (near-immutable) by a top-level family. Fact 3 — TIER (volatile: code matures) by a manifest field enforced by dependency lint, never by a path segment. Fact 4 — PROVENANCE (who may edit these bytes) by fixed subtree names inside each unit, at file granularity, never by a package-level field.

LAYOUT:

oak-open-curriculum-ecosystem/
  packages/                      MIT code, FLAT — tier is a manifest field, not a path segment
    result/                      tier:primitive                                                        [S1]
    safe-path/                   tier:primitive; security-critical flag routes extra review            [S2]
    curriculum-client/           tier:library — src/ hand wrapper + generated/ spec-derived types (trigger: upstream-spec, ~29x/yr)  [S4, P1-spec]
    curriculum-bulk/             tier:library — generated/ bulk schemas + snapshot (trigger: upstream-bulk, ~7x/yr)                 [P1-bulk]
    search-contracts/            tier:library — generated/ contracts (trigger: search-contracts, ~16x/yr)                           [P2]
    graph-corpus/                tier:library — src/ hand API + generated/ mined corpus data, 24MB (trigger: corpus-mine, ~19x/yr)  [S3, P2]
    codegen-pipeline/            tier:library — hand-written PRODUCER code only; every output it makes lands in some unit's generated/ subtree  [S7]
    search-store/                tier:library — generic datastore machinery, extracted                 [P10]
    search-retrieval/            tier:library                                                          [S6]
    design-tokens/               tier:library — src/ token definitions + generated/ CSS (trigger: token-build)                      [S5, P2]
    design-system/               tier:library — vendor/ byte-preserved third-party (hash-manifested, TRACKED) + src/styles/ hand-written  [P3]
    showcase-widget/             tier:surface — widget SOURCE; its build lands in demos/design-showcase/generated/widget/           [P11]
    obs-sentry/, obs-posthog/    tier:library                                                          [S8]
  content/                       OGL root partition — curriculum content units only
    curriculum-reference/        hand-curated reference data; MIT packages consume it as a workspace dependency, never absorb it    [P5]
  brand/                         reserved-licence root partition
    oak-brand-assets/            trademark imagery, hash-manifested; refresh tooling writes wholesale   [P6]
  apps/                          product surfaces — supported, full product gates
    curriculum-mcp/              [P9-product]
    search-cli/
  demos/                         published non-product — one-way barrier: import packages/, imported by nothing
    curriculum-hub/              [P9-demo]
    design-showcase/             generated/widget/ holds the built widget (trigger: widget-build, ~18x/yr)                           [P11]

MECHANISMS (the 'will anything tell me' answers):
1. Every generated/ subtree carries generated/.manifest.json: producer command, trigger event class (upstream-spec | upstream-bulk | search-contracts | corpus-mine | token-build | widget-build), inputs, measured cadence. A repo-level generation-graph check recomputes producer-to-output edges from all manifests each CI run and fails on orphan outputs, undeclared producers, or outputs stale against their declared inputs. Cross-unit edges (codegen-pipeline -> curriculum-client/generated; showcase-widget -> design-showcase/generated/widget) are first-class rows in this graph — that is the concrete answer to 'when I change this, what else must change'.
2. Edit boundary is positional and per-byte: src/ (and anything not otherwise claimed) = hand-editable; generated/ = machine-written — CI regenerates-and-diffs, so a hand edit fails the build with the producer named in the error; vendor/ and brand assets = byte-preserved — tracked in VCS with a hash manifest, any edit fails the hash check. No package-level editBoundary field exists, so there is nothing to drift and no 'Mixed' escape value.
3. Dependency lint recomputes tier edges (primitive imports no internal package; library imports primitive|library; surface imports any package) and audience arrows (apps -> packages; demos -> packages; nothing imports demos, ops, or research; demos never import apps).
4. Licence validator: package.json license must equal the unit's root-partition licence; a marker scan forbids OGL or brand-reserved content outside content/ and brand/. A unit that seems to need two licences is, by rule, two units joined by a workspace dependency.

organisingRules.name: Licence partitions the root
organisingRules.rule: Every unit lives under exactly one licence root: content/ is OGL-only, brand/ is reserved-only, every other root is MIT-only. No unit ever contains two licence classes; a genuine dual need becomes two units with a declared workspace dependency (code imports content, never absorbs it).
organisingRules.carrier: Top-level directory + package.json license field + CI validator that recomputes the root/field match per unit and scans for licence markers outside their root.

organisingRules.name: Provenance is a subtree, not a package attribute
organisingRules.rule: Inside any unit: src/ and unclaimed paths are hand-editable; generated/ is machine-written and any hand edit will be overwritten and CI-failed; vendor/ is byte-preserved third-party. An agent answers 'who may edit these bytes' from the path alone, at file granularity, at zero lookup cost.
organisingRules.carrier: Fixed subtree names + CI regenerate-and-diff for generated/ + tracked hash manifest for vendor/.

organisingRules.name: Every generated subtree declares its producer
organisingRules.rule: Each generated/ subtree carries a manifest naming the producer command, its trigger event class (upstream-spec | upstream-bulk | search-contracts | corpus-mine | token-build | widget-build), its inputs, and its measured cadence. A repo-level generation-graph check recomputes producer-to-output edges from the manifests and fails CI on orphan outputs, undeclared producers, or outputs stale against inputs — including cross-unit edges.
organisingRules.carrier: generated/.manifest.json per subtree + generation-graph CI check that recomputes, never merely records.

organisingRules.name: Audience families at the root
organisingRules.rule: apps/ is product (supported, full gates); demos/ is published non-product (one-way barrier); ops/ is operational tooling under its own lighter gate; research/ is isolated under its own gate. Arrows: apps and demos import packages/; nothing imports demos, ops, or research; demos never import apps.
organisingRules.carrier: Top-level family + package.json audience field + dependency lint that recomputes the arrows every CI run.

organisingRules.name: Tier is declared, not path-encoded
organisingRules.rule: packages/ is flat. Each unit declares tier: primitive | library | surface. Dependency lint recomputes allowed edges: primitive imports no internal package; library imports primitive or library; surface imports any package. Promoting or demoting a unit is a one-field edit plus a green lint run — the organisation's own cost of change is one line, because the volatile fact lives in the cheap carrier.
organisingRules.carrier: package.json tier field + dependency-lint check that recomputes edges from actual imports.

organisingRules.name: Vendored and brand bytes are tracked and hashed, never ignored
organisingRules.rule: vendor/ subtrees and brand/ assets are committed to VCS with a lockfile-style hash manifest; refresh tooling replaces them wholesale and rewrites the manifest; CI hash-check fails any hand edit. Byte-preservation is provable, and every refresh is a reviewable diff.
organisingRules.carrier: Tracked bytes + hash manifest + CI hash check.

fixDesign.notes: WHAT SURVIVES FROM THE AUDITED DESIGN: the tier concept with one-way import flow; the apps/demos split with a one-way barrier; isolated research and operational families; committing generated bytes to VCS; most individual probe homes. Those parts of the convergence are sound and are retained. WHAT THE FIX CHANGES AND WHY: (1) licence becomes a root partition with a recomputing validator, because the estate makes never-mixable a hard constraint and the audited design both violated it ('Mixed (per-export-path)') and hung it on a nonexistent npm mechanism; (2) edit boundary moves from a per-package field with a 'Mixed' escape to positional per-byte subtrees (src/ vs generated/ vs vendor/), because the estate's question is per-byte and the hottest units are exactly where 'Mixed' says nothing; (3) the three redundant axes (Generation Origin / Change Rhythm / Edit Boundary) collapse into one subtree-level provenance fact plus a per-subtree manifest, eliminating triple-declaration drift; (4) every declared fact gets a named check that recomputes it — generation graph, regenerate-and-diff, hash manifests, dependency lint, licence scan — so 'will anything tell me?' is answered by machinery, not convention; (5) tier is declared in the manifest rather than path-encoded, because pnpm name-based imports make the path a poor home for a volatile fact: reorganising a unit's tier costs one field edit, which is the honest answer to 'what does it cost when the organisation is wrong'. OPEN ITEM, PRICED NOT DECIDED: the 24MB corpus at ~19 refreshes/yr accrues roughly 450MB/yr of pre-packing history churn; the design keeps it in VCS for diffability and checkout reproducibility, but if growth doubles, moving graph-corpus/generated to an artifact store with a pinned digest in the manifest is a contained change because consumers import the package, not the bytes' path. MIGRATION HONESTY: P10 extraction and S7 decomposition are adoption steps of this design; the audited design scored its own P10 against the current layout instead of its target, which is why its probe table read as forced.

fixDesign.design:
Use stable, licence-homogeneous governed units rather than role/tier directories. The only semantic directory partition is the legally durable one:

units/
  mit/<stable-unit-id>/
  ogl/<stable-unit-id>/
  brand-reserved/<stable-unit-id>/

Every leaf is a pnpm/turbo-addressable unit or a data/artifact unit represented by a small build wrapper. Every unit has a schema-validated unit.yaml. Mutable facts—kind, audience, publication, support promise, gate profile, owner, external system, and architectural layer—remain metadata and generated views, so changing them does not move files. A unit is homogeneous for licence, edit authority, generation trigger, release/deployment promise, and gate profile. A difference in any of those properties requires separate units connected by typed edges.

unit.yaml records stableId, licence, editAuthority, owner, delivery, supportPromise, gateProfile, inputs, outputs, and typed edges. Edge types include imports, generatedFrom, embeds, readsAtRuntime, validates, deploysWith, and sharesExternalSystem. Each change-sensitive edge states whether a downstream rebuild, check, review, or coordinated release is required. A generated impact index gives agents one bounded document for discovery, while the distributed manifests remain authoritative.

Machine-owned units declare an event ID, generator unit and command, complete input and output inventories, and input/output digests. Byte-preserved units declare upstream provenance and an expected digest. CI maps every changed path to one unit, rejects unowned or wrongly edited bytes, verifies generated freshness, computes the affected reverse graph, and runs the declared checks. Product, demo, research, security-critical, generator, content, brand, and live-operations gate profiles are explicit; being outside product gates never means being unchecked.

The initial migration is acknowledged as expensive. Thereafter, ordinary reclassification changes metadata only. Splits and merges retain stable-ID aliases and use graph-derived rewrite tooling; licence changes remain deliberately expensive legal migrations.

organisingRules.name: Atomic governance boundary
organisingRules.rule: Split units whenever licence, edit authority, regeneration event, release or deployment promise, or gate profile differs. Different consumers alone do not split reusable logic; consumer-specific executables remain separate adapters.
organisingRules.carrier: Schema-validated unit.yaml plus a repository validator that rejects heterogeneous units.

organisingRules.name: Licence isolation
organisingRules.rule: MIT code, OGL content, and reserved brand assets must occupy separate units and legal roots. Per-path mixed licensing and mixed exports are forbidden.
organisingRules.carrier: units/mit, units/ogl, and units/brand-reserved roots; unit.yaml licence; CI file-inventory and dependency checks.

organisingRules.name: Single edit authority
organisingRules.rule: Every unit is exactly HumanOwned, MachineGenerated, or BytePreserved. Mixed is not a valid value.
organisingRules.carrier: unit.yaml editAuthority; path-to-unit index; generator or provenance attestations; changed-file CI enforcement.

organisingRules.name: Explicit regeneration contract
organisingRules.rule: Each generated unit has one named event, generator, input inventory, output inventory, and freshness test. Shared vendors or credentials do not imply a shared regeneration boundary.
organisingRules.carrier: generation section in the generated unit's unit.yaml and digest attestations produced by its turbo task.

organisingRules.name: Typed change graph
organisingRules.rule: Record compile, runtime, generation, embedding, validation, deployment, and external-system relationships. Each edge declares the consequence of a relevant upstream change.
organisingRules.carrier: unit.yaml edges and a generated reverse-impact index.

organisingRules.name: Impact enforcement
organisingRules.rule: For every change, compute affected units and require their declared rebuilds, checks, reviews, or coordinated releases. An unexplained multi-unit change fails validation.
organisingRules.carrier: Diff-to-unit mapper, impact command, turbo task selection, and CI status.

organisingRules.name: Orthogonal delivery promises
organisingRules.rule: Publication, audience, support promise, and runtime kind are independent fields; a unit may have multiple consumers without being assigned a hybrid class.
organisingRules.carrier: unit.yaml delivery, audiences, supportPromise, and kind fields.

organisingRules.name: Risk-based gates
organisingRules.rule: Assign explicit gates to all units. Research may use product-grade engineering gates without becoming a product; live operations use operational safety gates; security-critical primitives add security review.
organisingRules.carrier: Versioned gate profiles referenced by unit.yaml and expanded into turbo/CI tasks.

organisingRules.name: Stable addressing
organisingRules.rule: A unit's path contains only its durable licence class and stable ID. Architecture, maturity, audience, and ownership changes never require a move.
organisingRules.carrier: Stable unit IDs, generated indexes by facet, and alias records for genuine split or merge migrations.

organisingRules.name: Derived architecture
organisingRules.rule: Layers are computed from the typed dependency graph rather than encoded in paths. Cycles and forbidden runtime directions require narrow, expiring exceptions.
organisingRules.carrier: Graph validator, generated architecture view, and reviewed exception records.

organisingRules.name: External-system separation
organisingRules.rule: Units may share an external-system identifier and runtime credential while retaining distinct schedules, generators, licences, and failure domains.
organisingRules.carrier: externalSystem references in unit.yaml; secrets supplied outside version control.

organisingRules.name: Agent-efficient discovery
organisingRules.rule: An agent can answer where a path belongs, who may edit it, and what it affects without scanning the estate.
organisingRules.carrier: Compact generated path index, unit summaries, and reverse-impact index, all checked against authoritative manifests.

fixDesign.notes: The probe says P2 contains four generated collections, while the estate explicitly enumerates five generated artefact classes. The design therefore assigns all five named classes distinct homes instead of silently omitting or merging one. Cadence figures are recorded as observations, but event identity—not frequency—is the boundary. The legal roots intentionally encode only the durable constraint that cannot be reclassified cheaply; all other taxonomies are generated views. The design does not claim that the initial migration or a future licence change is cheap.

defects.claim: The design permits legally forbidden mixed-license units.
defects.evidence: The estate says MIT, OGL, and reserved-brand bytes are “never mixable in one unit.” The design nevertheless allows “Mixed (per-export-path)” and places P5 in a “dual license: MIT code + OGL content” unit. Its alternative placement is unresolved: “packages/docs/ or packages/core/reference-data/.”

defects.claim: It has no first-class change-impact or notification model.
defects.evidence: The governing question is what else must change and whether anything will report it, in an estate with 308 multi-unit commits per year. `regenerationTrigger`, CI naming conventions, directories, and ESLint imports do not declare reverse consumers, generated-from, embeds, serves, invokes, scheduled-refresh, or release-together relationships, nor required proofs for them.

defects.claim: Its edit classification cannot identify who may edit each byte.
defects.evidence: A unit-level `editBoundary: Mixed` only acknowledges ambiguity. P3 relies on `.gitignore`, which is neither an edit prohibition nor protection for tracked files. S5 labels the whole token pipeline Generated although only its CSS output is stated to be generated. No exact path-to-authority, producer, command, input, or freshness contract is delivered.

defects.claim: The proposed unit-boundary rule is neither deterministic nor applied to the hard cases.
defects.evidence: The design says units differ by generation origin, edit permission, and change coordination, but gives no mandatory split rule. P1 combines spec and bulk flows with different schedules and mechanisms; S7 preserves spec fetch, type generation, corpus mining, and hand curation in one unit; P4 and P12 retain different consumers and failure modes in an `agent-tools` catch-all.

defects.claim: P2 is not actually placed.
defects.evidence: “Multiple units (sdk-codegen, oak-design-tokens, etc.)” does not name all four artefact collections, their four event classes, their producers, or their consumers. `etc.` cannot support the claimed `forcedFit: false`.

defects.claim: P11’s defining cross-unit relationship is erased.
defects.evidence: P11 requires widget source, built output, and a different serving unit. The proposed placement puts `dist/widget.js` in the showcase unit and identifies no separate serving unit, embed edge, digest, or freshness check.

defects.claim: P8 is factually redefined and deprived of appropriate assurance.
defects.evidence: The current probe describes scripts that operate against live systems and sit outside product gates. The design recasts them as “bootstrap-time only,” with “no ESLint lint” and no import contract. Outside product gates does not mean outside operational safety gates.

defects.claim: Quality and failure-policy boundaries are absent.
defects.evidence: P7 must receive product-equivalent quality checks without shipping; P8 needs operational checks; P9 carries a different support promise; S2 is security-critical. None of the six classifications declares an enforceable gate profile or failure policy.

defects.claim: Human accountability is absent despite an AI-majority workforce under human ownership.
defects.evidence: No classification or carrier names an accountable human owner, approval boundary, or authorised generator. “HandWritten” describes provenance, not permission or accountability.

defects.claim: The primary directory taxonomy makes ordinary reclassification expensive and offers no migration seam.
defects.evidence: Tier, audience, domain, and lifecycle are encoded in roots such as `core`, `sdks`, `apps`, `demos`, and `research`. The design itself concedes path changes are O(n) and layer changes are “very expensive,” while providing no stable unit IDs, path-independent references, aliases, or affected-consumer migration mechanism.

defects.claim: The dependency policy is ambiguous and too narrow for the estate.
defects.evidence: The arrow `core ← libs ← sdks/apps ← demos` is undefined and appears inconsistent with the stated rule blocking demo-to-app imports. ESLint import checks cannot govern generation, file embedding, CLI invocation, scheduled jobs, runtime calls, deployment, or Turbo task coupling.

defects.claim: The actual classification system is overlapping and differs from its summary.
defects.evidence: The summary promises import-boundary, quality-gate, consumption, domain, licence, and edit-domain dimensions. The delivered six omit import boundary, quality gate, and domain. Generation Origin and Change Rhythm largely duplicate each other; Demo and Research appear in both Consumer Class and Stability; S6 is classified “Published/Internal dual” despite those being presented as alternative values.

defects.claim: Package-level carriers cannot cover the proposed estate.
defects.evidence: The dominant descriptor says `unit-kind=package`, and most classifiers live in `package.json`, yet the layout also treats `.husky`, `.ds-sync`, individual runtime scripts, assets, and research trees as organisational units without a universal manifest.

defects.claim: The product/demo distinction is visible but not enforceable as a support contract.
defects.evidence: Separate `apps/` and `demos/` roots survive scrutiny as a useful signal, but `privateFlag`, `publishConfig`, and one import rule do not encode deployment eligibility, support promise, promotion approval, or product-quality requirements.

defects.claim: P10 remains unresolved and contradicts the elite claim.
defects.evidence: The summary claims “zero forced fits,” while P10 is explicitly `forcedFit: true`. Its generic datastore machinery remains embedded in the product and is merely described as “extractable,” which postpones rather than supplies a placement.

defects.claim: The generated-file policy is internally inconsistent.
defects.evidence: The summary says generated bytes are committed under `/data` or `/generated` and mentions `.generation.yaml`; the actual design uses package internals, `dist/widget.js`, unspecified CSS locations, and `.gitignore`. No manifest schema or validator appears in the classifications or layout.

defects.claim: Several carriers assert conclusions rather than proving them.
defects.evidence: README prose, `0.x` versus `1.x`, CI hook naming, custom package fields, and an exports map asserted to carry per-path licensing have no stated schema, validation, or enforcement mechanism.

defects.claim: Some placements invent publication status and vendors not established by the grounding.
defects.evidence: S3 becomes Published and Stable from only “74 public symbols”; S6 becomes Published/Internal although publication was not given; S8 names two specific vendors although the probe supplies one unspecified commodity-vendor adapter.

fixDesign.design: Use stable, licence-homogeneous units plus an explicit impact graph. A unit is an atomic ownership, verification, and delivery contract—not necessarily an npm package. Physical layout is `units/<legal-class>/<stable-id>/`; every unit has a validated `unit.yaml`, while generated `unit-index` and `impact-graph` views provide discovery. Only the legally durable class and stable identity affect the path. Role, domain, maturity, publication, product/demo/research/operations status, and gate profile are independent manifest facts. A split is mandatory when legal class, accountable owner, independent refresh trigger, release/support promise, or failure/gate policy differs. Human source and generated output may coexist only when they are mechanically rebuilt and delivered atomically and every path has an exact authority rule; otherwise the output is a separate artifact unit. Consumers are derived from typed graph edges rather than guessed from directory names.

organisingRules.name: Stable identity and discovery
organisingRules.rule: Every unit receives an immutable ID. Cross-unit imports and non-code references use that ID or its stable package export, never relative traversal. Mutable classifications do not cause directory moves.
organisingRules.carrier: `units/<legal-class>/<stable-id>/unit.yaml`, plus generated `.estate/unit-index.json` mapping IDs to locations.

organisingRules.name: Deterministic unit boundary
organisingRules.rule: Split whenever legal class, accountable owner, independent trigger/schedule, release or support promise, or gate/failure policy differs. Extract genuinely shared implementation into a capability unit and put consumer-specific behaviour in adapters.
organisingRules.carrier: A versioned manifest schema, boundary validator, and owner-approved split/merge record.

organisingRules.name: Licence purity
organisingRules.rule: Each unit has exactly one legal class. Mixed and per-export licensing are rejected. Cross-licence units may read or serve separately identified payloads but may not copy them into another unit. Release assemblies preserve component provenance.
organisingRules.carrier: Legal-class directory root, `legalClass` manifest field, file inventory, and package/bundle provenance validation.

organisingRules.name: Exact byte authority
organisingRules.rule: Every tracked path is classified as human-authored, generated, or synchronized/vendor-preserved. Machine-managed paths name their producer, inputs, command, trigger, tool version, and freshness proof. Direct edits without regeneration evidence fail validation.
organisingRules.carrier: Non-overlapping `authority.paths` rules in `unit.yaml`; regeneration receipts or deterministic regenerate-and-diff checks; checksums for byte-preserved vendor payloads.

organisingRules.name: Typed impact relationships
organisingRules.rule: Declare imports, generated-from, reads, embeds, serves, invokes, validates, deploys, and release-together edges. Every edge states what a change requires: regenerate, rebuild, retest, review, or release together, plus the proof task.
organisingRules.carrier: `edges` entries in unit manifests and generated `.estate/impact-graph.json`.

organisingRules.name: Affected-work enforcement
organisingRules.rule: Map changed paths to units, compute the reverse impact closure, report it locally, and fail CI when required proofs or co-change obligations are missing. Reconcile observable package, import, and Turbo edges with the declared graph.
organisingRules.carrier: An impact query command, changed-file CI gate, Turbo proof tasks, and graph-consistency validator.

organisingRules.name: Dependency direction
organisingRules.rule: Unit-level import and generation graphs must be acyclic. Shipping surfaces may depend on capabilities and artifacts, but not on demo, research, or operational adapters. Demo, research, and operations units may reuse supported capabilities. A generic capability may not depend on a product surface.
organisingRules.carrier: Typed edge-policy matrix enforced against imports, package dependencies, generated inputs, and build tasks.

organisingRules.name: Separate delivery facts
organisingRules.rule: Publication, support promise, delivery kind, gate profile, and criticality are independent fields. Product deployment requires a product support contract; demos cannot silently acquire it; research can use product-equivalent gates while remaining non-shipping; live operations use an operational-safety profile.
organisingRules.carrier: `humanOwner`, `role`, `publication`, `support`, `delivery`, `gateProfile`, `criticality`, and nonsecret `externalRefs` fields, enforced by deployment and credential policies.

organisingRules.name: Complete custody
organisingRules.rule: Every tracked file belongs to exactly one unit. Tool-required root files are declarative shims with an exact owning unit; executable logic remains in that unit. Unowned or multiply owned files fail validation.
organisingRules.carrier: Repository file-to-unit inventory and manifest `mountedPaths` for unavoidable root entry points.

organisingRules.name: Bounded reorganisation cost
organisingRules.rule: Changing domain, maturity, audience, publication, or support metadata does not move files. Moving a unit updates one ID-to-path mapping. Splits and merges use temporary aliases and the impact graph to enumerate consumers. Legal reclassification remains deliberately expensive because it requires a real audit.
organisingRules.carrier: Stable IDs, generated workspace/build configuration, alias records with expiry, and graph-derived migration plans.

probePlacements.probe: P1: interface-spec snapshot and bulk dataset from one service
probePlacements.placement: Two independent chains: `mit/curriculum-spec-fetcher` → `<verified-spec-class>/curriculum-spec-snapshot`, and `mit/curriculum-bulk-fetcher` → `ogl/curriculum-bulk-snapshot`. They retain separate 29/year and 7/year triggers while referencing the same nonsecret service and credential handle.

probePlacements.placement: Separate machine-payload units and producers: `mit/curriculum-api-types` (~29/year), `mit/search-contracts` (~16/year), `<verified-schema-class>/bulk-schemas` (~7/year), and `ogl/mined-corpus` (~19/year). Each has its own generated-from edge, trigger, and freshness proof. The widget is the fifth generated class handled by P11.

probePlacements.probe: P3: byte-preserved vendor files plus handwritten styling
probePlacements.placement: `<verified-vendor-class>/vendor-style-snapshot` is synchronized and checksum-protected; `mit/handwritten-styles` is human-authored. A consuming surface references both without merging their custody.

probePlacements.probe: P4: tooling serving interactive, commit-time, and scheduled consumers

probePlacements.placement: `ogl/reference-data` contains data only. Any parser, validator, or accessor remains in a separate MIT unit connected by a `reads` edge.

probePlacements.placement: Extract to `mit/commodity-search-core`. The product-specific pipeline and `search-retrieval` unit depend on it; the generic unit cannot import product-specific policy.

probePlacements.probe: P11: widget source, built output, and different serving unit
probePlacements.placement: `mit/widget-source` → `mit/widget-bundle` through a generated-from edge. The separate serving unit has an `embeds`/`serves` edge to the bundle's stable ID and verified digest; CI checks bundle freshness.
