`mit/result`, with zero dependencies, explicit compatibility proofs, and reverse-impact reporting for its high fan-out.
`mit/safe-path`, with a security-critical gate profile, accountable owner, incident-derived invariants, and affected-consumer security tests.

probePlacements.probe: S3: graph-data library with about 74 public symbols
probePlacements.placement: `mit/graph-data`. Its exported surface is recorded as a contract, but external npm publication is not inferred from symbol count; publication remains an independent owner-declared fact.

`mit/curriculum-client`, declared as a public supported package, depending on the separate generated `curriculum-api-types` unit. Spec changes trigger type regeneration and client compatibility proofs.

probePlacements.probe: S5: design-token source, compiler, and generated CSS
probePlacements.placement: `mit/design-token-source` and `mit/design-token-compiler` produce the machine-owned `mit/design-token-css` artifact unit. Every consuming surface has an explicit edge to the CSS unit.

probePlacements.probe: S6: search-retrieval library over a commodity datastore
probePlacements.placement: `mit/search-retrieval`, depending on `mit/commodity-search-core` and, where required, `mit/search-contracts`. Internal consumers and publication status remain separate facts.

Dissolve it rather than rename it: separate spec fetcher/snapshot/type-generator/types, bulk fetcher/snapshot/schema-generator/schemas, corpus-miner/mined-corpus, and OGL curated-reference units. Their manifests and typed edges provide the pipeline view without recreating a mixed-trigger monolith.
`mit/observability-adapter-<provider-id>`, one unit per actual provider, with no invented provider names and no product-policy dependency.

fixDesign.notes:
What survives from the attacked design: product and demo really do require distinct support contracts; brand assets require their own legal unit; research and operations need explicit isolation; tiny primitives, a public curriculum client, generic search machinery, and thin commodity adapters are plausible boundaries; declarative generation manifests are the right idea once made complete and enforceable.

The replacement costs more manifests and produces more artifact units. That is deliberate where the prior monolith concealed independent schedules, legal classes, or failure policies. Generated indexes keep discovery cheap for agents. A genuinely semantic but undeclared edge remains the main residual risk; static dependency reconciliation and review of recurring multi-unit changes can expose candidates, but no directory taxonomy can infer every coupling.

The packet does not establish the licence of the fetched interface specification, derived bulk schema, or third-party vendor files. Their `<verified-...-class>` placements are therefore explicit intake gates, not guesses. Unknown legal status blocks ingestion rather than permitting a mixed unit. No repository or filesystem content was read.

instrumentDefects.claim: The task statement names the incumbent answer's form in its own words, and the FORBIDDEN list then names its title — so the survey cannot distinguish an agent that derived a basis from an agent that was told to produce one.
instrumentDefects.evidence: The task demands "the minimal set of independent classifications it rests on". A minimal independent spanning set is the definition of a basis. The FORBIDDEN list bans "any file whose name mentions census, inventory, basis, reorganisation, taxonomy, survey, or deconstruction" — the ban list is a keyword hint that names the incumbent artefacts (a census producing a basis producing a taxonomy). The instrument forbids reading the document while restating its central concept verbatim in the instruction.

instrumentDefects.claim: The probe set does not test the design; it supplies the classifications. Every case is a minimal pair that names its own discriminating dimension in the case text, so the facet list is handed over before the agent designs anything.
instrumentDefects.evidence: P1 supplies "refreshed on different schedules by different mechanisms"; P2 "each rebuilt in response to a different event class"; P3 "must never be hand-edited, alongside hand-written styling that changes freely"; P4 "several distinct consumers on different rhythms (interactive commands, commit-time guards, scheduled jobs)"; P5/P6 licence and "reuse terms"; P7/P8 gate regime; P9 "different audiences and support promises"; P10 generic vs product-specific; P12 states the answer outright — "the same change rhythm, different consumers and failure modes". Read in order, these dictate roughly {editability, regeneration trigger, consumer, rhythm, licence, gate regime, genericity, audience} — precisely the set the survey will report as convergent.

instrumentDefects.claim: The probe set is the forbidden census delivered through the front door, already abstracted. The abstraction step is where the whole design decision lives, and the instrument performs it for every agent identically.
instrumentDefects.evidence: S1–S8 are singular and definite, with census-grade precision no design exercise needs: "~74 public symbols", "The estate's largest unit", "born from a security incident", "published publicly". These are measurements of specific existing units. Choosing to describe a case as "a path-safety utility born from a security incident — small, security-critical" rather than by its domain, its importers, or its build is itself a classification, already made by the instrument's author. An agent forbidden to read code can never re-cut that abstraction, so it can only reproduce the vocabulary it was issued. (Corroborated externally: the estate's top level — agent-tools, apps, demos, ds-bundle, research, runtime-only-scripts, packages/{core,libs,sdks,design} — maps case-for-case onto P3, P4, P7, P8, P9, P12 and S1–S8, so a "good" placement score reproduces today's tree.)

instrumentDefects.claim: forcedFit is a one-way error term: it can only ever record a failure of the design, never a failure of the instrument. Misfit is attributed to the respondent by construction.
instrumentDefects.evidence: "mark forcedFit true where your design has no natural home for it" — the boolean is defined entirely as a property of the design ("your design has no natural home"). The schema offers no value and no field for: the case is mis-posed, the two halves are not comparable, the stated facts are unverifiable, the placement is deliberately plural, or my design dissolves the question. A survey whose owners fear the instrument teaches the answer has built the one field that could have detected it as a confession of respondent error.

instrumentDefects.claim: The schema closes every extension point, so every form of disagreement must be smuggled into two free-text strings that the structured fields will outrank at coding time.
instrumentDefects.evidence: "additionalProperties":false appears at all three levels (root, organisingRules items, probePlacements items). There is no field for rationale, confidence, assumptions, alternatives considered, evidence the agent would need, tradeoffs accepted, or critique of the instrument. The gradeable, comparable part of the output is exactly the part whose shape the instrument fixed; the part the agent is free in ("design", "notes") is the part that cannot be compared across the fleet.

instrumentDefects.claim: The free-form variant is not a control. It disclaims the answer's shape in one sentence and re-imposes it in the next, shares the structured schema, and has the critique channel removed.
instrumentDefects.evidence: "Do not assume the answer is a classification scheme, a directory tree, or any particular kind of structure" is followed immediately by "State what determines where any given piece of code lives and how anyone (human or machine) would check the organisation is being followed" — location and checkability, the two presuppositions just disclaimed. Only one output schema is supplied for both variants, and it requires organisingRules and probePlacements with forcedFit. And the free-form variant drops the structured variant's "name any question you believe this task statement should have asked but did not" — the arm most likely to attack the framing is the arm denied the channel to do it. Naming the two structures it forbids also primes them.

instrumentDefects.claim: The A/B/C manipulation is confounded: B changes valence and frame, not just concern cardinality, so no difference involving B can be attributed to the stated variable.
instrumentDefects.evidence: The header calls the variants "3, differing in concern cardinality", but A and C are headed "WHAT THE ORGANISATION MUST SERVE" (positive, question-shaped, C a strict superset of A) while B is headed "WHAT THE ORGANISATION MUST PREVENT" (negative, narrative failure modes). The design is actually one nested dosage contrast (A⊂C) plus one reframe (B), reported as a single axis.

instrumentDefects.claim: Variant C's questions map one-to-one onto the classifications the fleet will emit, so any finding of the form "more concerns produce more classifications" is a tautology of the prompt text.
instrumentDefects.evidence: C asks "Who may edit these bytes, and what regenerates them?" (editability/provenance facet), "May this piece import that one?" (layer facet), "Under what terms may this leave the estate — freely, under a content licence, or never?" (licence facet), "Which rules are checked by a machine, and which exist only as good intentions?" (enforcement facet). Each question is answerable by exactly one facet, and the task then asks for "the minimal set of independent classifications". C is the answer key written in interrogative mood.

instrumentDefects.claim: The estate statistic that most constrains the design is stated in the incumbent's own units, so it is only meaningful under the partition the survey claims to be putting in question — and no field lets an agent say so.
instrumentDefects.evidence: All three prose variants assert "three hundred and eight touch several units at once". "Units" presupposes an existing, countable partition; under any different partition the number is undefined. It is presented among neutral facts (file count, commit count) as though equally partition-independent. Since reading is forbidden, no agent can recompute it at path granularity, and the schema has no field to challenge a premise.

instrumentDefects.claim: The instrument asks licence and reuse questions while forbidding the artefacts that carry licence terms, so those probes can only be answered by accepting the instrument's assertion of the fact it is measuring.
instrumentDefects.evidence: P5 ("a content licence different from the code around it"), P6 ("reuse terms differ from everything else") and C ("Under what terms may this leave the estate — freely, under a content licence, or never?") sit alongside a ban on "ANY Markdown file anywhere in the repository" and "anything under docs/". Licence, attribution and branding statements are exactly the Markdown the ban covers. The design is scored on honouring a fact it is structurally prevented from verifying.

instrumentDefects.claim: "Monorepo" is asserted as a fixed premise in the first sentence of both variants, foreclosing the whole family of answers that changes the repository boundary.
instrumentDefects.evidence: Structured: "how a TypeScript monorepo estate should be organised into units of code". Free-form: "how a TypeScript monorepo estate should be organised — whatever 'organised' should turn out to mean". The free-form arm's invitation to redefine "organised" does not extend to "monorepo"; splitting the estate, extracting published units to their own repositories, or vendoring boundaries are unavailable in the arm advertised as unconstrained.

instrumentDefects.claim: A contested cost model is asserted as an estate fact, tilting the design toward layout-as-index and foreclosing designs where locating is a tool operation rather than a traversal.
instrumentDefects.evidence: B: "A machine collaborator, which pays for every file it opens, burns its whole budget just discovering where things are." C: "What does it cost a machine collaborator, paying for every file it opens, to find one unit?" This conflates opening with locating; agents with glob, grep, and index tools locate without opening. The claim is stated in the fact-bearing prose, not offered as an assumption to be argued with, and no field exists to argue with it.

instrumentDefects.claim: Prose B asserts consensus that a reorganisation is needed, which forecloses the null result — the finding a survey worried about its own suggestiveness most needs to be able to record.
instrumentDefects.evidence: "the reorganisation everyone agrees is needed is priced so high by the current layout that it simply never happens." An agent concluding "the present organisation is adequate; change nothing" is told the question is settled, and is asked to "produce a complete organisational proposal" regardless. This assertion appears only in B, adding a third uncontrolled difference to the A/B/C contrast.

instrumentDefects.claim: Several probes carry the instrument's verdict inside the case description, so an agent that disagrees is arguing against an adjective rather than a fact.
instrumentDefects.evidence: P10: "Generic machinery, reusable against any similar datastore, currently embedded inside a product-specific pipeline" — "currently embedded" pre-labels the state as a defect awaiting extraction. S7: "a codegen pipeline mixing spec-fetch, generated types, corpus mining, and hand curation" — "mixing" pre-labels cohesion as impurity. An agent holding that S7 is correctly one unit, or that P10's machinery should stay put until a second consumer exists, must first dislodge the framing, with no field for doing so.

instrumentDefects.claim: The carrier menu is a closed list presented as examples, and it pre-blesses one derivation while omitting the mechanisms a dissenting design would reach for.
instrumentDefects.evidence: "the concrete carrier for each (directory level, name convention, manifest field, enforcement rule, derived from the dependency graph)" — five options, mirrored by the schema's single required "carrier" string. Absent: ownership metadata, git co-change history, licence files, tests, human review, deployment boundary, workspace/package boundary, generated index. "Carrier" itself presupposes that a classification must be materialised somewhere; and one string per rule cannot express a distinction carried jointly by a directory, a manifest field and a lint rule.

instrumentDefects.claim: "placement" is a single string, which collides with the one probe whose correct answer is two homes — the schema fights its own probe.
instrumentDefects.evidence: P11: "A browser-built interactive widget whose BUILT OUTPUT is embedded and served by a different unit than its source." P1 has the same shape (one source, two artefacts on two rhythms). The schema's probePlacements item permits one "placement" string and one boolean; a two-home answer must be compressed into prose or misreported as forcedFit.

instrumentDefects.claim: Enforcement is presupposed as the mode of compliance, so "deliberately unenforced" is not a statable position.
instrumentDefects.evidence: The task's fourth question is "how the rules are enforced", and the schema requires organisingRules items to carry a "carrier". C asks "Which rules are checked by a machine, and which exist only as good intentions?" — framing unchecked rules as "good intentions", i.e. as failure. A design holding that at this size enforcement cost exceeds its benefit, or that review is the right check, has no field shaped for it.

instrumentDefects.claim: The single compliance control is an unparseable self-report with the desired answer supplied in the instruction.
instrumentDefects.evidence: "In notes, state how many repository files you read (zero if none)" — the count lands in the same free-text "notes" string as the "question that should have been asked" and any protest, so it cannot be extracted mechanically; "(zero if none)" anchors the socially correct answer; and "You have never seen this estate's current plans or analyses" asserts a knowledge state the instrument cannot verify. Honour-system isolation is not a measurement when the harness's own tool log could supply it.

instrumentDefects.claim: The output artefact is not self-describing: nothing records which task statement or which prose variant produced it, in a factorial survey with at least six cells.
instrumentDefects.evidence: The schema's required keys are "design", "organisingRules", "probePlacements", "notes" with "additionalProperties":false, so an agent cannot even volunteer its arm. Any mis-join in the harness is undetectable from the artefacts, and the arm-level findings the survey exists to produce rest entirely on out-of-band bookkeeping.

instrumentDefects.claim: Probe identity is an unconstrained string, so case completeness and case identity cannot be validated, despite the instruction to place every case.
instrumentDefects.evidence: "probe":{"type":"string"} with no enum, while the probe set says "place every case". Twenty cases (P1–P12, S1–S8) can be silently dropped, merged, or renamed, and the boolean forcedFit rate — the survey's headline number — is computed over a denominator the schema does not fix.

foreclosedAnswers: Change the repository boundary: split the estate, or extract published units into their own repositories. "TypeScript monorepo estate" is a fixed premise in the opening clause of both variants, including the one advertised as unconstrained.

Organise by domain or bounded context (curriculum, search, design, agent tooling). No probe uses domain as its discriminating dimension, so a domain design must mark forced fits across most of P1–P12 while a facet design scores clean — the case set penalises it by construction.

Reject facets altogether: hold that the right organisation is a single hierarchy, or a set of deliberately dependent and overlapping distinctions. "the minimal set of independent classifications it rests on" fixes plurality, orthogonality and minimality before any design work begins.

Deny that a partition exists at all: propose derived views computed on demand from the dependency graph and co-change history, with no durable unit boundary. "where units live", "the layout it implies", "placement" and the free-form arm's "what determines where any given piece of code lives" all require a spatial home.

Allow a file or case to belong to several groupings at once. probePlacements items carry one "placement" string, and "what makes two things separate units" presupposes a pairwise decidable, disjoint partition.

Hold that organisation should be advisory — carried by review and convention, unenforced because enforcement costs more than it saves. "how the rules are enforced" plus the required "carrier" field, plus C's framing of unchecked rules as "good intentions", leave no shape for it.
Conclude that the current organisation is adequate and nothing should change. Both task statements demand a proposal, and B asserts "the reorganisation everyone agrees is needed".

Accept periodic re-rooting as cheap and design for it, rather than designing to avoid it. C asks "How does the organisation absorb a doubling of the estate without re-rooting?", making avoidance the goal rather than one option.

Reject the per-file discovery cost model on the grounds that agents locate by index and search, not by traversal. It is asserted twice as estate fact ("paying for every file it opens") with no field for challenging a premise.

Point out that "three hundred and eight touch several units at once" is defined only under the incumbent partition and is therefore unusable as evidence for a different one. It appears in all three prose variants as a neutral fact, and reading the estate to recompute it is forbidden.

Say that a probe is mis-posed, internally inconsistent, or unverifiable — for instance that P5's and P6's licence claims cannot be checked because every licence document is Markdown and therefore banned. forcedFit only accuses the design; no field accuses the case.

Say that a case dissolves under the proposed design — that P12's guards and validators, or P7's study code, are not units at the grain the design works at. The only available signal is forcedFit, which reads as the design failing rather than the question not arising.
Give a case two homes (P11's source and its built output; P1's spec snapshot and bulk dataset). One placement string per case.
Report confidence, state which claims are guesses, or name the evidence that would change the answer. No field exists, and "additionalProperties":false blocks adding one.

Argue that S7 is correctly a single cohesive unit, or that P10's generic machinery should stay embedded until a second consumer appears. The case text pre-labels them "mixing" and "currently embedded", so the disagreement must first dislodge an adjective.

Attack the instrument at all, in the free-form arm: it drops the structured arm's invitation to "name any question you believe this task statement should have asked but did not", leaving critique to compete with the file-count attestation inside one "notes" string.
result.betterInstrument:
Sketch of an instrument that could actually detect what this one asserts.

FIRST, FIX THE ARMS. Three variables are currently entangled: how much the prompt reveals about the answer's FORM, how many concerns it names, and whether concerns are framed as goals or as failures. Make them three independent factors and cross them deliberately. Form-revelation should have a genuine zero level: an arm whose prompt contains none of the words units, classification, taxonomy, basis, carrier, layout, minimal, or independent, asking only "here is the estate and what people need from it; say how it should be organised, in your terms." Cardinality should vary by nesting only (A strictly contained in C, as now). Valence should be a separate binary crossed with cardinality, so a three-concern failure-framed cell and an eleven-concern goal-framed cell both exist. B as written cannot support any inference about cardinality.

SECOND, ELICIT BEFORE REVEALING. Run two sealed phases. Phase 1 gives the estate facts and the concerns and asks for the organisation in the agent's own vocabulary, with a self-declared list of "the distinctions my design makes" — agent-named, agent-counted, no cases in sight. Phase 1 output is sealed and un-editable. Phase 2 then reveals the cases and asks for placement. Convergence measured on phase-1 vocabulary is real; convergence measured after twenty pre-abstracted minimal pairs is an echo. The present instrument only has a phase 2, and reports it as though it were a phase 1.

THIRD, SHIP EVIDENCE, NOT ABSTRACTIONS. Every case should arrive as raw material — a directory listing, a package manifest, an importer count, the first thirty lines of two source files, the licence header if there is one — with no adjectives and no diagnostic nouns. Never "byte-preserved", "machine-regenerated", "different event class", "currently embedded", "mixing". Deciding that a thing is best described by its regeneration trigger rather than by its domain IS the design decision; handing that description over pre-made means the survey measures recall, not design. If the live estate must stay unread, ship a redacted evidence bundle rather than a forbidden-word list — a ban list that includes "census", "basis" and "taxonomy" is a hint, not an isolation mechanism. Enforce isolation in the harness by denying reads, and measure compliance from the tool log rather than from a self-reported number.

FOURTH, BALANCE THE CASE SET. For every dimension the instrument suspects, include a case where that dimension is the WRONG cut: two things that differ on it but plainly belong together, and two that agree on it but plainly do not. Add cases whose natural discriminator is domain, ownership, deployment target, team, or test strategy, so a non-facet design is not scored as forced-fit by construction. Include at least two decoys whose correct answer is "these are not units at all" and one case with a deliberately inconsistent description, to see who notices. A case set in which every case names its own axis is a specification, not a probe.

FIFTH, MAKE MISFIT TWO-SIDED. Replace the boolean with a closed disposition: natural, forced, multiple (list the homes), dissolved (my design makes the question not arise), underdetermined (I cannot place this without evidence X — name it), misposed (the case's stated facts are inconsistent or unverifiable — say how). Require a becauseOf field naming which of the design's own distinctions did the placing; that is the only field that tests whether the stated organisation does any work, and the current schema has no link at all between rules and placements.

SIXTH, LET THE ANSWER BE SHAPELESS AND RECORD ITS SHAPE. Drop "organisingRules" with its required name/rule/carrier. Take instead a free-text organisation, a unitOfOrganisation string that may say "there is no unit; the organisation is a derived view", and a mechanisms array of {claim, whatItDecides, howItIsChecked, checkedBy: automated|review|convention|nothing, costToChange}. An empty mechanisms array must be legal with an accompanying whyNone. "Carrier" presupposes materialisation; "checkedBy: nothing" is the field that lets an agent say a rule is deliberately unenforced.

SEVENTH, OPEN THE FIELDS THAT CARRY DISSENT. Require, as first-class keys rather than free-text scraps: assumptionsIChallenge (quoted spans of the instrument the agent believes are wrong), confidence per major claim, alternativesRejected with reasons, evidenceIWouldNeed, and instrumentCritique separate from the compliance attestation. Make filesRead an integer and pathsRead an array. Record the arm inside the artefact so it is self-describing. Do not set additionalProperties:false on the root — a survey afraid of teaching its answers must leave a door for the answer it did not imagine.

EIGHTH, STOP ASSERTING CONTESTED FACTS. Report co-change at path granularity, not as "commits touching several units", so it survives any partition. Present the per-file agent cost model as a hypothesis the agent may reject, not as an estate fact. Remove "the reorganisation everyone agrees is needed", and make "the current organisation is adequate" an explicitly permitted verdict with a field to carry it.

NINTH, ADD A CALIBRATION ARM AND PRE-REGISTER THE FAILURE CONDITION. Run one cell whose case set comes from a different estate with a different natural cut. If the fleet returns the same distinctions for both estates, the instrument is generating the answer, not the estate. Then state in advance what result would count as the instrument having taught the answer — for example, cross-arm agreement on distinction count and names above a stated threshold, or phase-2 vocabulary overlap with the case text above chance — because without a pre-registered failure condition, a survey cannot report a negative finding about itself, and this one currently cannot.

descriptors.name: pathLoad
descriptors.values: How many classifications the directory tree is made to carry. path-heavy = 3 or more encoded in the tree (audience + generality/tier + provenance and/or licence roots). path-light = exactly 1-2 in the tree (typically licence and/or promise, plus reserved provenance segments inside a unit), everything else in a validated manifest. path-null = flat namespace; the path encodes unit identity only (or a universal null partition such as units/), with classification carried entirely by manifests, name-grammar tokens, and a generated index.

descriptors.name: assurance
descriptors.values: Highest verification rung the design names a mechanism for. stated = conventions/config only, declarations trusted (UNOCCUPIED in this corpus). recomputed = at least one fact reconstructed from primary evidence (dependency graph from real imports, manifest/path agreement, licence file scan, workspace totality). reproduced = additionally proves non-authored bytes by re-running the producer and diffing, or by digest-pinning vendored bytes. self-correcting = additionally carries a measured signal over history or the build graph (co-change pairs, multi-unit-commit rate, per-unit cache-hit) that can declare a boundary wrong and propose merge/split.

cells.whyElite: The only member that knows which rung it is on. Four axes (coupling tier, audience/support, artefact provenance, shipment membership) each with exactly ONE named carrier, and it tests axis independence against the probe set rather than asserting it. Grounded in 28 real manifests; provenance is carried by fixed leaf names plus turbo outputs plus the deliberate ABSENCE of a package.json for vendored trees, which is the sharpest use of a non-carrier in the corpus. Its own closing note names the gap that keeps it off the higher rungs -- 'a tariff schedule with no inspector at the gate is a wishlist' -- so it is honest about lacking byte proof rather than implying it. Runners-up B-haiku-0 and B-terra-38/39/40 cover similar ground with weaker carrier discipline.

The modal cell of the whole corpus, and this is the entry that refuses to let it be lazy. Its binding rule -- 'a boundary with no interlocking behind it is not a boundary, it is paint' -- forces every one of five classifications to name a concrete instrument (regenerate-and-diff drift gate, vendor hash-pin, credential-scope scan, hook-registration check, dependency-cruiser edge rules). It is also the only tiered design that marks a probe forced BECAUSE ITS OWN INSTRUMENT CANNOT SEE THE CASE (P10: generic machinery mis-embedded before extraction is invisible to any gate it can name) rather than because the case is homeless -- diagnosis of its own blind spot, not of the probe. Close contenders: B-sonnet-3 (grounded, finds live estate defects such as the published SDK's restricted access field and the ground-truths licence mismatch) and B-sonnet-4 (cleanest statement of what does NOT split: audience and support promise are metadata, never topology).

Resolves the cell's central tension -- a tree that carries a lot must still be cheap to change -- by pricing each carrier against the VOLATILITY of the fact it holds: licence (immutable) gets a root partition, audience (near-immutable) a top-level family, TIER (volatile, because code matures) is evicted from the path into a manifest field enforced by dependency lint, and provenance drops below unit level into fixed subtrees at file granularity. That single eviction is the most consequential structural correction anywhere in the tiered family, and it keeps the falsifier: boundary-fitness telemetry (multi-unit-commit rate against a ~5% baseline, per-unit export counts, per-exposure closure weights) reported as signal, never as an automatic gate. B-fable-9 is the strongest alternative and contributes the corpus's one genuine repair to the co-change metric itself -- generator-driven fan-out commits are EXEMPT, so a regeneration event cannot poison the boundary-health number.

The tightest carrier economics in the corpus. Path carries only what must never be violated (licence root; edit-ownership as a second segment with exactly three values and NO 'Mixed' escape, because mixing is resolved at directory level rather than named at unit level); everything mutable sits in one schema-validated manifest with one fact per carrier. Its decisive rule is negative and nobody else states it: NO RULE IS KEYED ON A PATH GLOB -- import policy, gates, ownership and licence all read manifests and the resolved dependency graph -- so moving a unit changes no rule, no config and no import specifier, which is the only mechanical answer in the corpus to 'what does it cost when the organisation is wrong'. The gate recomputes rather than reads (regenerate-and-diff plus provenance digests that include externally fetched inputs), and it declares two honest forced fits instead of smoothing them. B-opus-6 and O-seeded-29 are the strongest from-scratch members; both reach the same shape independently from a grounded reading, which is itself corroboration.

The only design that carries a rule which DELETES a classification: every change-trigger value must be bound to a detectable event (schedule, webhook, upstream changelog, vendor release, named decision area), and any value nobody can point a detector at is deleted within a quarter and its units merge. That is minimality enforced rather than professed. It also sets numeric falsifiers on its own boundary set (multi-unit-commit rate ceiling of ~7% against the measured 5.2% baseline) and sequences its own migration correctly -- manifest fields and validators in REPORT-ONLY mode first, licence-forced splits next, trigger splits after, directory moves last because they are cheapest. O-seeded-30 is the best cost model in the corpus (a terminal charges for moves, not storage; the 308 multi-unit commits are the re-handles) and ratchets a re-handle budget as a merge gate.

Answers the flat family's real weakness. A flat namespace makes RECLASSIFICATION free but makes RE-ADDRESSING expensive, and this is the only member that prices that directly: a unit is an atomic ownership/verification/delivery contract (explicitly 'not necessarily an npm package'), it carries an immutable stable ID that is independent of its editable display slug, its published package name and its physical location, and splits/merges retire IDs through alias records rather than rewriting consumers. It also gives the strongest byte-authority formulation in the cell -- non-overlapping exact path-authority rules per unit, with regeneration receipts or deterministic regenerate-and-diff and checksums for byte-preserved payloads -- plus typed impact edges (generates, embeds, serves, invokes, release-together) each stating what a change REQUIRES, so cross-unit obligation is computed rather than remembered. T-grade3-47 and X-seeded-36 are close; both additionally evict regenerated payloads from version control into a digest-pinned external store.

The most complete occupant of the corpus's best-defended corner: flat units/*, all classification in a validated manifest, plus a measured falsifier. Three things nobody else assembles together. (a) A sharp byte-durability test -- 'can this be reproduced byte-exactly from tracked inputs alone?' -- which evicts every derived artefact from version control WITHOUT the naive reading that would also delete lockfiles (a lockfile names external world state, so it is a decision record, not an output), and which honestly names the cost it creates: the estate must own an immutable content-addressed mirror or it has traded tracked bytes for unbuildable clones. (b) A hazard-token name grammar carrying only the four irreversible facts (ogl, reserved, vendor, demo) with an explicit clause that no rule may read any other part of a name -- the guard that stops a name grammar quietly becoming the directory tree again. (c) Discovery reframed as a query rather than a path, on the correct argument that a tree is a one-dimensional projection of a seven-dimensional classification and always loses six. Its closing section is the most honest in the corpus: with directories carrying nothing, a misclassification is invisible to the eye and every ounce of weight now rests on the checks -- if they are weak the design is decorative. D-free-53 is the strongest alternative and contributes the single most original mechanism anywhere here: per-unit turbo cache-hit rate as a free, continuous, honest measurement of boundary quality.

outliers.why: Not a design. A grouping derived mechanically from 12 months of git co-change (union-find at 0.5, >=5 shared commits) with no carrier, no rule, no naming scheme and no enforcement. It cannot be placed on either descriptor because it declines to encode anything anywhere. Its value is as a control: its clusters cut ACROSS boundaries almost every design draws -- it groups the search CLI with two SDKs, and agent-tools with the error primitive -- i.e. measured behaviour does not respect the app/package seam that the tiered family treats as foundational.

Not a design, and the archive's sharpest falsifier. Derived purely from 146 workspace-level import edges: a substrate tier of five high-in-degree units, then TWO small domain clusters (graph, design-tokens) and one residual blob of 21 units. The import graph therefore supports one substrate plus a blob -- it does not support the multi-level core/libs/sdks/design hierarchies that 24 entries in the modal cell encode in their paths. No descriptor position, because it carries no classification at all.

Singular in kind rather than in position. It declines to produce a unit taxonomy at all: 'organisation is a regeneration and ownership choreography problem, not a directory tree problem'. Its object is authority over bytes and refresh cadence (four ownership classes keyed to who regenerates and on what schedule), verified procedurally by a regeneration registry, a nightly regenerate-and-diff, a licence audit and file-header trigger metadata. It has no unit-boundary rule, no naming scheme and no placement procedure, so neither descriptor can read it -- it answers a different question from the other 66 and answers it coherently.

reducerX.notes:
ARCHIVE SHAPE. 7 occupied cells of 12 possible; 66 designs placed, 3 outliers. The distribution is heavily lopsided and that lopsidedness is the finding: 24 of 66 (36%) sit in path-heavy/reproduced -- a tiered tree plus regenerate-and-diff plus NO way to learn the boundary is wrong. Add path-heavy/recomputed and the tiered family is 34 of 66 (52%). The frontier cells are thin: path-light/self-correcting has 3 members, path-heavy/self-correcting has 4.

THE EMPTY RUNG. No entry sits at `stated`. Every design in the corpus names at least one mechanical carrier (lint config, turbo task graph, manifest schema, dependency-cruiser). The floor of this population is already CI-checked; the variance is all above that line. I kept `stated` in the descriptor because its emptiness is informative.

THE FEEDBACK MINORITY. Only 13 of 66 (20%) carry a measured falsifier. Three distinct mechanisms appear: multi-unit-commit rate against the estate's own 308/5,900 = 5.2% baseline, usually with a stated ceiling (B-opus-7 ~7%, B-opus-8 ~6%, O-grade3-62 ~8%); pairwise co-change matrices proposing merges and splits (B-sonnet-5, X-seeded-37, O-seeded-31, D-free-54); and per-unit turbo cache-hit rate (D-free-53, unique in the corpus, and the cheapest of the three since it is already being measured). One design repairs the metric before using it: B-fable-9 exempts generator-driven fan-out commits, without which ~89 regeneration events a year poison the number.

WHERE THE CORPUS ARGUES WITH ITSELF. The pathLoad axis is not my imposition -- it is the estate's live dispute, argued explicitly by at least a dozen entries. The strongest form of the argument is volatility-pricing: put a fact in the path only if changing it should be an expensive, visible move (licence, edit-ownership), and put every fact that legitimately changes during a unit's life (tier, audience, support promise, gate profile) in a manifest. F-grade3-63 and K-opus-1-fix state this most clearly; O-grade3-62 and B-opus-8 push it to its limit by removing classification from the path entirely and paying for it with a generated index plus a query interface.

FORKS I DECLINED TO PROMOTE. Two real, recurring, orthogonal forks that I could not classify reliably across all 66 and so left out of the descriptor space. (1) Generated artefacts as their own units (generated/, artifacts/, materials/generated/, or manifest-only artifact units) versus reserved subtrees inside the owning unit (gen/, .generated/<event-class>/). It correlates loosely with pathLoad: path-null designs tend toward artefact units, path-light designs toward lanes. (2) Whether regenerated bytes are committed-and-guarded or EVICTED from version control into a digest-pinned external store -- roughly 8 entries evict (O-grade3-62, X-seeded-36, T-grade3-47 among them), and only O-grade3-62 supplies a test sharp enough to avoid deleting lockfiles along with them.

DUPLICATES INFLATE THE MODAL CELL. B-terra-38/39/40 are byte-identical to each other; T-grade2-44 and T-grade3-48 are identical; D-free-55 and B2-terra-61 are identical; B-fable-9 and B2-fable-59 are near-identical; F-grade3-63 and K-fable-1-fix are near-identical. About 6 entries are relay/transport artefacts rather than independent designs, and they cluster in the tiered region -- so the true concentration in path-heavy is slightly lower than the raw count suggests, though the ranking of cells is unchanged.

GROUNDING DOES NOT MOVE THE SHAPE. Grounded entries (those that read the estate) land in the same cells as ungrounded ones. What grounding changes is content, not structure: it produces live findings (a published SDK whose publishConfig contradicts its stated intent; hand-enumerated package tuples in a boundary lint rule that the dependency graph already knows; a build-cache incident caused by a value absent from a task's env list) and it lets a design cite evidence for its axes rather than assert them. Two independently grounded opus designs (B-opus-6, O-seeded-29) converged on the same path-light shape, which is the corpus's only case of convergent structure from independent evidence.

PLACEMENT CONFIDENCE. Cell membership was assigned on the dominant carrier signal in each design's stated layout plus the highest assurance mechanism it names with a concrete instrument. Elites were verified line by line against their design text. A handful of bulk placements in the two largest cells (B and F) are judgement calls at the recomputed/reproduced margin -- specifically where a design says a hook 'checksums generated files' without naming a comparison target. I resolved those downward to `recomputed`, so the reproduced cell is if anything under-counted.

descriptors.name: path-semantics
descriptors.values: How much classification the directory tree itself carries: taxonomic-zones (many semantic top-level zones — role/audience/licence/provenance encoded in the tree, sometimes nested by domain); axis-rooted (exactly one or two deliberately chosen axes in the path — promise, licence, reach, or distribution roots — everything else in manifests); flat-namespace (single-level unit directories, path carries identity only; includes the stricter no-subdirectory 'files-only' variants); incumbent-tuned (keeps or annotates the estate's existing apps/demos/packages tiering, proposing corrections rather than a new tree); no-layout (organisation stated as invariants, process, or contracts — the tree is a mere rendering or absent).

descriptors.name: generated-byte-custody
descriptors.values: Where machine-regenerated artefacts live: committed-verified (tracked in git, guarded by regenerate-and-diff, checksums, or provenance manifests); excluded (payloads banned from version control — build caches, artifact stores, manifest-only artifact units, pins); durability-split (an explicit per-artefact test or flag decides tracked vs external — diffability, trigger decoupling from consuming commits, size/offline-need, or a checkedIn field).

descriptors.name: boundary-feedback
descriptors.values: How the design learns its own boundaries are wrong: rule-static (declared rules and validators only; boundary revision is manual judgement); telemetry-governed (a standing instrument with named metrics, thresholds, or cadence — co-change/multi-unit-commit rate, re-handle budget, pressure ledger, scheduled generality-promotion job — proposes merges and splits on an ongoing basis).

cells.whyElite: The most complete instance of the modal design: five classifications each proven pairwise-independent, architectural binding verified from dependency closure rather than asserted, an explicit producer/output-custody rule, per-consumer entrypoint doctrine, human accountability and credential scoping, and zero forced fits achieved by stating what it refuses to split on (size, cadence, shared credentials) rather than by vagueness. Runner-up: B-sonnet-4, whose use of S7 as the design's own stress test is the sharpest single move in this cell.

Cleanest coupling of a zoned layout to an empirical governor: four genuinely independent axes on the workspace-package substrate, generator-driven fan-out commits exempted from the multi-unit-commit health metric so the signal stays honest, merge/split verdicts surfaced for ratification rather than auto-executed, and validators that emit the violated rule plus its cure for an agent workforce.

Sole owner of the transient-asset law in a zoned tree: an artefact is committed iff its regeneration event is decoupled from the commits that consume it — a decidable test that gives the five artefact classes their own docks (one per trigger, each with a regeneratedBy contract) while same-commit derivations stay build products.

The strongest single design in the corpus: every carrier choice is justified against observed drift in the real estate (hand-enumerated boundary tuples, name/path disagreements, turbo override sprawl), one-fact-one-carrier is enforced by checks that recompute from primary evidence rather than trusting declarations, reclassification costs exactly one edit per axis, and it names its own costs (heterogeneous core, index rot risk, scaffold burden). The three falsifier fixes in this cell independently converge on its licence-rooted, recompute-everything shape.

Smallest declared classification set in the corpus (three axes plus one derived measurement) that still resolves every probe; boundary quality is converted into one ratcheted number (the re-handle budget seeded at the measured 5.2%), every invariant is a machine-decidable predicate, and genericity/size/criticality are explicitly refused as address-worthy facts. Runner-up: B-opus-7, whose falsifier set and trigger-to-detector binding are nearly as sharp.

Singleton and deservedly so: the carrier-selection rule (path only for facts whose change should be a visible reviewed move), materialisation-by-diffability (committed only when the diff is the change signal, otherwise fetched by pinned hash), a cohesion auditor as the design's built-in falsifier, and honest forced-fit accounting — it names where its own five axes are thinnest (P6 egress, S2 riding on the promise axis).

The most complete flat-namespace contract model: seven contract dimensions per unit, one-read discovery via a generated units index, typed code and artefact relations, per-unit readFirst/workflow commands budgeting agent navigation, and mechanical split/merge with stable-ID aliases and expiring exceptions so reorganisation stays cheaper than a taxonomy re-root. (X-seeded-34, T-grade1-43, T-grade2-45 are the radical files-only sub-flavour of this cell.)

Unique constitutional machinery on top of a flat estate: a rule with no validator is void by construction (Article XIV empties the category of unenforced intentions), amendment classes carry graded ratification costs so law and enforcement can never disagree in a window, the pressure ledger is how the constitution notices it is wrong, and the deep-import ban makes reserved unit interiors real. Runner-up: B-opus-8, whose imports-UNION-declared-edges coupling graph is the best answer in the corpus to 'will anything tell me?'.

Makes the no-tracked-generated-bytes regime actually operational rather than a .gitignore aspiration: generated collections become manifest-only artifact units with producer edges, immutable external storage, and provenance verification before consumption; the form--domain--capability name grammar carries orientation without a tree, and a single policy engine with thin per-consumer tool units enforces the whole scheme.

The sharpest custody test in the corpus — byte-exact reproducibility from tracked inputs — cleanly separating derived (never tracked), received (pin tracked, bytes only if offline-stable), and authored, while saving lockfiles from a naive reading; it prices the immutable mirror the constraint creates instead of hiding it, limits name semantics to four irreversible hazard tokens with a meta-rule stopping names becoming a covert tree, runs a co-change ceiling (8%) as feedback, and is openly suspicious of its own zero forced fits.

Best evidence discipline of the incumbent-tuners: 30 manifest-only reads, the tier pattern verified three independent times before being made law, two live carrier defects surfaced (publishConfig.access contradicting the published-client intent; a single MIT licence field over hand-curated content), and it identifies the release/version boundary as a missing organising axis with concrete lockstep-vs-independent evidence. Runner-up: F-seeded-32, whose kept/razed/regretted accounting of the existing city is the most decision-legible narrative in the cell.

Only member: reframes organisation as regeneration-authority and licence choreography — a regeneration registry, nightly regenerate-and-diff, licence audit, and quarterly graph audit — with the directory tree explicitly demoted to non-authority. Thinnest of the no-layout family but internally coherent.

States the objective function nearly every other design leaves implicit — minimise bytes an agent must read to make one correct change — then makes boundary quality measurable with two free signals (leak-rate classification of the 308 multi-unit commits; per-unit turbo cache-hit rate, with the 24MB corpus named as the live suspect). Its insistence that licence purity be checked on the published artefact, not src/, catches the failure that source-tree checks miss.

outliers.why: Not a design at all: a union-find over measured commit co-change with a threshold. No unit definition, no carriers, no custody or enforcement policy — every descriptor except boundary-feedback is undefined for it. Valuable only as a calibration baseline for the telemetry-governed cells (its groups are the empirical answer those designs' co-change instruments would converge toward).

Same status as MECH-cochange from the other data source: hub separation plus label propagation over the measured import graph. It produces a grouping, not an organisation — no normative content, no answer to any of the probe questions — so it cannot occupy a cell in a space whose dimensions are design commitments. Useful as the graph-side calibration counterpart.

reducerY.notes: Derivation: the obvious candidate dimensions — WHICH axes a design classifies on — turned out not to discriminate: licence class, provenance/edit-authority, audience/promise, regeneration trigger, and assurance profile appear in nearly every one of the 67 designs, and almost all converge on the same probe verdicts (split S7, isolate OGL/brand into own units, keep P4/P12 as entrypoints not units, split P1 by trigger). What genuinely varies is (1) how much of the classification the path itself carries, (2) custody of regenerated bytes, and (3) whether boundary revision is instrumented — hence the three descriptors. 13 of 30 possible cells are populated. Notable structure: the modal design (taxonomic zones, committed generated bytes, static rules) holds 21 of 67 members and is where every terra walker and most haiku/codex output lands. Mode collapse in the terra tier is severe: B-terra-38/39/40 are byte-identical across three groundings, T-grade2-44 equals T-grade3-48, B2-terra-61 repeats the same design, and D-free-55 (nominally free-form) embeds it again — six near-copies of one design across supposedly independent runs, which inflates that cell. Grounding correlates with layout: grounding-a (repo-read) runs dominate incumbent-tuned; the flat-files and excluded-bytes cells are largely prompt-variant-induced (the X/T/grade-3 arms carried flatness and no-VCS constraints), so those cells measure constraint-following quality more than free invention. The four falsifier fixes independently converge on licence-rooted paths plus recompute-not-record gates, i.e. on O-seeded-29's territory — corroborating that region of the space. Free-form origin is the only source of the no-layout cells. Strongest overall members if a single winner were wanted: O-seeded-29, O-seeded-30, O-grade3-62, B2-opus-58, D-free-53 — notably all share one meta-commitment: carriers chosen by cost-of-being-wrong, checks that recompute, and a named falsifier for the design itself."

alignments: Both reducers independently chose "how much classification the directory path itself carries" as their PRIMARY axis despite building unrelated vocabularies from scratch: X's pathLoad (heavy/light/null) and Y's path-semantics (taxonomic-zones/axis-rooted/flat-namespace/incumbent-tuned/no-layout) partition the same corpus along essentially the same underlying gradient. This is a real convergence on which dimension matters most -- not a schema artifact, since the corpus schema never asks for a 'pathLoad' concept at all.

Both independently flag MECH-cochange and MECH-imports as non-design measurement controls that occupy neither descriptor space, with near-identical framing (X: 'its value is as a control... measured behaviour does not respect the app/package seam'; Y: 'valuable only as a calibration baseline for the telemetry-governed cells'). Both agree these are calibration artifacts, not organisational proposals.

Both independently detect and warn about the same specific near-duplicate / mode-collapse cluster inflating the modal cell's raw count: B-terra-38/39/40 byte-identical; T-grade2-44=T-grade3-48; D-free-55=B2-terra-61; B-fable-9~B2-fable-59; F-grade3-63~K-fable-1-fix. X: 'DUPLICATES INFLATE THE MODAL CELL... about 6 entries are relay/transport artefacts.' Y: 'Mode collapse in the terra tier is severe... six near-copies of one design across supposedly independent runs.'

Both independently isolate D-free-52 as a genuine singleton outside their descriptor space, quoting or paraphrasing its 'regeneration and ownership choreography problem, not a directory tree problem' framing almost verbatim, and both note it has no unit-boundary rule at all so neither descriptor can read it.

Both independently converge on the same substantive probe-level verdicts drawn from the underlying design content -- S7 (the codegen mega-package) splits by trigger/provenance in essentially every elite description in both reductions; OGL/brand content gets its own unit; P4/P12 stay as entry-points inside one tool package rather than splitting on consumer rhythm alone. Y states this explicitly ('almost all converge on the same probe verdicts'); X's per-cell whyElite text shows the identical pattern independently.

Both find that falsifier-origin entries (K-*-fix) cluster tightly together rather than scattering: X groups K-opus-1-fix, K-codex-1-fix and K-sol-1-fix in one 6-member cell (path-light/reproduced); Y groups the same three in its corresponding 6-member cell (axis-rooted/committed-verified/rule-static) with identical membership. Independent agreement on this specific sub-population's cohesion is a real convergence, directly relevant to the basin-mass question.

Both note that grounded (repo-reading) entries produce the same live, estate-specific findings without those findings changing which shape-family a design belongs to -- X: 'grounding does not move the shape... it produces live findings... it lets a design cite evidence rather than assert it'; Y's incumbent-tuned cell (populated overwhelmingly by grounding-a entries) is itself evidence that grounded designs correct-in-place rather than invent a structurally different shape.

mismatches.xView: X uses exactly 2 orthogonal axes (pathLoad x assurance), a 3x4 grid of 12 possible cells, 7 occupied.
mismatches.yView: Y uses 3 axes (path-semantics x generated-byte-custody x boundary-feedback), a 5x3x2 grid of 30 possible cells, 13 occupied.
mismatches.finding: The two reducers disagree on how many independent dimensions this corpus supports. Y explicitly argues the 'obvious' candidate axes (licence class, provenance/edit-authority, audience/promise, regeneration trigger, assurance profile) turned out NOT to discriminate because nearly all 67 designs already agree on them, and lands on 3 different axes instead; X keeps a 4-rung assurance ladder rather than collapsing it to Y's binary. This is a genuine disagreement about the corpus's true dimensionality, not a corpus-schema artifact.

mismatches.xView: X's second axis is a 4-level ladder (stated < recomputed < reproduced < self-correcting) measuring how much a design's own checks prove, with 'stated' explicitly empty across the whole corpus (a finding X calls out as informative).
mismatches.yView: Y's boundary-feedback axis is a binary (rule-static vs telemetry-governed) measuring only whether a standing measured signal governs boundary revision; verification-rigor questions are folded into Y's separate custody axis instead.
mismatches.finding: The two schemes decompose the same underlying corpus signal differently -- X conflates 'does a check recompute state' with 'does a signal revise boundaries' into one ladder, Y separates them into custody (recompute) and feedback (revise) as two axes. X's empty-'stated'-rung finding has no counterpart in Y's binary, and Y's clean rule-static/telemetry-governed split has no counterpart in X's ladder.

mismatches.xView: X places K-fable-1-fix in path-heavy/reproduced -- inside the corpus's modal, dominant-shape cell (24 members).
mismatches.yView: Y places K-fable-1-fix in axis-rooted/committed-verified/telemetry-governed, and states explicitly that 'the four falsifier fixes independently converge on... O-seeded-29's territory' -- the licence-rooted, NON-dominant corner.
mismatches.finding: The two reducers disagree about whether this single design belongs to the dominant shape or the minority licence-rooted shape. This is the one falsifier entry that could anchor the dominant cell, so the disagreement materially changes the basin-mass calculation: under X's reading falsifier entries contribute 1/4 to the dominant cell, under Y's reading 0/4.

mismatches.xView: path-null (flat namespace; the design's units/<realm>/<domain>/<slug>/ tree is read as carrying only unit identity, path carries nothing else).
mismatches.yView: taxonomic-zones (the same design's realm/domain/slug tree, with realm drawn from a 9-value controlled vocabulary, is read as carrying substantial semantic classification).
mismatches.finding: A same-design, cross-reducer disagreement on the single dimension both schemes treat as primary. Not resolvable by appeal to the corpus's forced schema fields, and it bounds confidence in any single-design shape call drawn from either reduction alone -- flagged as a contested row in the attractor test.

mismatches.aspect: Does grounding move the resulting shape?
mismatches.xView: X states directly: 'GROUNDING DOES NOT MOVE THE SHAPE... What grounding changes is content, not structure.'
mismatches.yView: Y states: 'Grounding correlates with layout: grounding-a (repo-read) runs dominate incumbent-tuned; the flat-files and excluded-bytes cells are largely prompt-variant-induced.'
mismatches.finding: Apparent contradiction resolves on inspection rather than being a true clash: Y's claim is about grounding-a specifically correlating with a category (incumbent-tuned) that only exists in Y's finer descriptor scheme -- X has no equivalent value to register the same correlation, so X's claim is true within its coarser scheme while Y's is true within its finer one. This is itself evidence that a reducer's descriptor vocabulary can suppress a real correlation simply by lacking a category for it.

mismatches.aspect: Elite selection in the modal / near-modal cells
mismatches.xView: X's elite for the path-heavy/reproduced modal cell (24 members) is S-seeded-24; X's elite for the path-light/reproduced cell (6 members, the licence-rooted corner) is the falsifier entry K-opus-1-fix.
mismatches.yView: Y's elite for the near-identical taxonomic-zones/committed-verified/rule-static modal cell (21 members) is B-sol-50 (an unseeded walker); Y's elite for the corresponding axis-rooted/committed-verified/rule-static cell (6 members, same membership as X's path-light/reproduced) is O-seeded-29 (a walker, not the falsifier entry).
mismatches.finding: Despite near-identical cell membership in the licence-rooted corner, the two reducers pick different single best exemplars, and neither reducer picks the same design as elite of the modal cell either (S-seeded-24 vs B-sol-50). Elite selection is not a settled, cross-reducer-stable judgment even where cell membership itself agrees closely -- a finding about the instrument's subjectivity at the point of ranking, not just at the point of classifying.

Headline grounding-b row; squarely in both reducers' dominant/modal cell.

Departs on the feedback axis in X and on both pathLoad and feedback in Y. Sonnet's grounding-b sibling (B-sonnet-4) DID match, so sonnet splits by grounding condition -- consistent with the instruction that grounding a/c rows are supporting only, not separable from sampling variance.

Opus's grounding-a run already departs to the licence-rooted axis-rooted/path-light corner, consistent with opus's grounding-b departure below -- opus resists the attractor at every grounding sampled.

Both reducers agree this one is flat/null -- codex's highest-concern variant (C) departs cleanly, unlike its variant-B sibling which is contested.

observations.shape: X:path-heavy/reproduced (modal cell, not X's elite) | Y:taxonomic-zones/committed-verified/rule-static (modal cell, Y's ELITE)
observations.note: Sol's only entry (n=1, no B2-sol counterpart, per instructions). Y names this the single best exemplar of the whole 21-member modal cell; X does not select it as elite for the equivalent cell (X's elite is S-seeded-24) -- shape agreement plus an elite-selection disagreement.

Second grounding-b sample for haiku; matches, giving haiku a clean 2/2 at the headline column. Raw design text was not included in the supplied corpus data -- shape inferred solely from X/Y cell membership, not independently verified against source.
