Either way it lands in the modal family. Shape inferred from reduction membership only.

attractorTest.verdict: On the headline grounding-b column (n=2 per tier except sol, n=1; 13 observations total), 9 of 13 (69%) are clean matches to the dominant 1a shape: haiku 2/2, sonnet 2/2, codex 2/2, terra 2/2 (discount-flagged as mode-collapse), and sol 1/1. Two tiers show a STABLE, PAIRED departure rather than noise: opus is 0/2 (both B-opus-7 and B2-opus-58 land in the path-light/axis-rooted, self-correcting/telemetry-governed corner -- the same corner opus's grounding-a run, B-opus-6, also lands in, so opus resists the attractor at every grounding sampled, not just b); fable is 2/2 PARTIAL (both B-fable-9 and B2-fable-59 match on the pathLoad/zone dimension but add a telemetry-governed feedback loop the dominant shape does not have). Counting fable's partial as a match-on-primary-dimension gives 11/13 (85%); counting it strictly as a non-match gives 9/13 (69%). The within-tier PAIRED consistency (both grounding-b samples in a tier always land in the same cell or cell-family) is the strongest evidence here: it means the departures are not single-sample noise, they are tier-conditioned. The attractor is real and strong but not universal -- it is resisted specifically and reproducibly by the opus tier, and partially reshaped (zone kept, feedback loop added) by the fable tier. Grounding-a and grounding-c rows are broadly consistent with this pattern (opus departs at grounding-a too; haiku/fable/terra match at grounding-c) but include one CONTESTED case, B-codex-12, where X and Y disagree on whether the design is heavy/taxonomic or null/flat at all -- which bounds confidence in the cleanliness of any single non-headline observation.
attractorTest.caveats: Tier, grounding, and sampling variance are not separable outside the grounding-b column: with n=1 (grounding a, grounding c per tier/variant) it is impossible to distinguish 'this tier reliably resists the attractor' from 'this specific sample happened to land elsewhere once.' The six B2-* rows are inferred solely from X's and Y's reduction cell-membership listings -- their full design text was not included in the corpus data supplied to this analysis, so their shape could not be independently verified against source the way the eighteen B-* rows were; this is flagged per verify-dont-trust rather than silently assumed. The B-codex-12 contested placement (X: path-null; Y: taxonomic-zones) demonstrates the underlying instrument is not fully reliable at the per-design level, which bounds confidence in any single 'match'/'no-match' call drawn from only one reduction. 'matchesDominant1aShape' is my own interpretive synthesis across two differently-shaped descriptor schemes (X's 2-axis grid vs Y's 3-axis grid), not a fact recorded directly by either reduction -- I defined 'matches' as landing in the heavy/taxonomic(or incumbent-tuned)+committed-verified+rule-static family on BOTH reducers' readings, and scored genuinely mixed cases (fable) as non-match on the strict reading while noting the partial-match alternative in the verdict.

basinMass.withFalsifierFixes: X (2-axis scheme): the 'tiered family' X itself names (path-heavy/recomputed + path-heavy/reproduced) = 34 of 66 placed designs = 51.5% (X rounds to 52%). This 34 includes 1 falsifier entry (K-fable-1-fix, in path-heavy/reproduced). Y (3-axis scheme): the modal cell alone (taxonomic-zones/committed-verified/rule-static) = 21 of 67 = 31.3%, containing ZERO falsifier entries. Broadened to include Y's incumbent-tuned/committed-verified/rule-static cell (the same family in its correction-flavoured sub-variant, 8 members, also zero falsifier entries) = 29 of 67 = 43.3%.
basinMass.withoutFalsifierFixes: Removing all 4 falsifier-origin entries (K-opus-1-fix, K-codex-1-fix, K-sol-1-fix, K-fable-1-fix) from both numerator (where present) and denominator: X's tiered family becomes 33 of 62 (34 minus the 1 falsifier entry it contained, over 66 minus all 4 falsifier entries in the corpus) = 53.2%. Y's modal cell becomes 21 of 63 (unchanged numerator, since none of the 4 falsifier entries were ever in it) = 33.3%; broadened family becomes 29 of 63 = 46.0%. THE HEADLINE FINDING: removing falsifier entries does NOT shrink the dominant-shape basin mass in either reduction -- it ticks UP slightly in every calculation (X: 51.5%->53.2%; Y modal: 31.3%->33.3%; Y broadened: 43.3%->46.0%), because 3 of the 4 falsifier entries (all 4, on Y's reading of K-fable-1-fix) anchor the ALTERNATIVE licence-rooted axis-rooted/path-light corner, not the dominant cell. This directly contradicts the premise that falsifier entries 'reading the prior elite verbatim' would be propping up the dominant shape's apparent size -- empirically they mostly anchor a different, non-dominant corner instead, and their removal is basin-mass-neutral-to-slightly-positive for the dominant shape.

comparator.decoyAnalysis: "None of the four decoy outputs (haiku, sonnet, opus, terra) reproduce the prior round's dominant shape. DECOY-haiku produces a plain layered architecture (entry/app/domain/shared by directory depth-1) with no licence zones, no generated/vendor split, no audience-tier split -- because the decoy estate has none of those facts to carry. DECOY-sonnet produces a flat app/+packages/* cohesion-clustered layout on three axes (consumption/cohesion/direction), again with no licence or provenance zoning. DECOY-opus is the sharpest test: at the highest tier, facing the corpus's own dominant-shape-producing prompt scaffold, it produces the MOST elaborate and most explicit REJECTION of the tiered/multi-package/licence-zoned shape -- 'One package. Zero workspaces... Licence (MIT, no exceptions)... Stated once... no per-file SPDX headers... no generated/ root (nothing is generated)' -- and supplies four explicit, falsifiable tripwires (a second deployable with divergent deps, an external consumer, conflicting dependency versions, or gate-time pain) for when a package boundary would become warranted. DECOY-terra likewise stays single-package and feature-organised, explicitly deferring workspace packages until 'an independently versioned, reusable, or separately runnable boundary' exists. VERDICT: this is a clean falsification of the strongest form of the convention-prior hypothesis (blind stamping of the tiered/licence-zoned/generated-committed shape regardless of territory) -- all four tiers correctly read the decoy estate's absence of multiple licence classes, generated artefacts, external services, and multiple deployment audiences, and did not manufacture directory zones or generated/vendor subtrees to carry facts that don't exist there. This weighs toward 'the dominant shape is territory-responsive,' at least on the dimensions this decoy varies. CAVEAT: the test only rules out the strongest (blind) form of the convention-prior hypothesis. It does not rule out a weaker, still-real form -- a strong LEARNED convention keyed to genuine surface features (multi-licence, generated bytes, multi-audience, external services) that correctly suppresses itself when those features are absent and correctly fires when they're present, without that convention constituting an independently-derived, first-principles analysis of THIS estate's specific territory each time. The decoy test cannot distinguish 'the model reasoned about this specific estate's needs' from 'the model correctly pattern-matched which convention applies to which estate shape' -- both produce the same observed behaviour here."
comparator.variantLeakage: "Global balance (6/6/6 across A/B/C) does not hold within the grounding-c WALKER subset the task asks to examine: only 7 grounding-c walkers exist across 6 tiers (haiku:A, sonnet:B, opus:C, fable:A, codex:B and codex:C, terra:C), giving an observed 2/2/3 split for A/B/C respectively, not 6/6/6 -- the balance is a whole-corpus property (including seeded, falsifier, and other-origin entries at grounding c) that does not survive restriction to walkers only. More importantly, tier and variant are almost perfectly confounded at n=1 per tier within this subset: every tier except codex contributes exactly ONE grounding-c walker at exactly one variant, so there is no way to hold tier constant and vary concern-cardinality within five of the six tiers. Codex is the sole within-tier comparison available (variant B, B-codex-12: 11 organisingRules entries vs variant C, B-codex-13: 12 organisingRules entries) -- a difference of one rule, too small to distinguish a real cardinality effect from noise. Using organisingRules-array length as a proxy for 'classification count' across all 7 grounding-c walkers: variant A (3 concerns) averages ~9 rules (B-haiku-2:7, B-fable-10:11); variant B (7 concerns) averages ~8.5 rules (B-sonnet-5:6, B-codex-12:11); variant C (12 concerns) averages ~10.3 rules (B-opus-8:13, B-codex-13:12, B-terra-40:6). There is a mild upward tilt from A/B toward C, but it is swamped by tier-driven variance: opus and codex tend to produce longer rule lists regardless of variant, and terra produces a FIXED 6-rule template (byte-identical to its own grounding-a and grounding-b entries) totally insensitive to variant -- B-terra-40 sits at the corpus's highest-concern variant (C, 12 concerns) yet has the LOWEST rule count of any grounding-c walker, actively working against the hypothesis. A second proxy, forced-fit count per probe placement, shows no clean trend either (A: 2 total forced fits across 2 designs; B: 0; C: 1 across 3 designs) -- if anything mildly inverted relative to concern cardinality. VERDICT: no confident leakage signal is detectable in this walker population. The n is too small (2-3 designs per variant, mostly n=1 per tier-by-variant cell) and confounded with strong tier effects (verbose tiers like opus/codex, template-locked tiers like terra) to separate a genuine concern-cardinality effect from ordinary tier-driven and sampling variance. Tier-by-variant cells must be treated as confounded at their n, exactly as instructed."
comparator.priorDescriptorFit: "Partial fit: the prior tuple's ENUM VALUES mostly transfer onto this corpus, but its predicted DOMINANT CELL does not accurately describe this round's distribution, and it is missing an entire axis this round's evidence needed. Point by point: (1) Cardinality -- prior found 5-6 dominant; this corpus's walkers mostly self-report 4-7 axes (B-sonnet-4: four axes, B-sol-50: five classifications, B-opus-6/B-fable-9: six axes, B-codex-12/13: seven), which overlaps the prior's band -- FIT. (2) Primary tree carrier (role/family/stratum/clock/authorship/flat/other) -- this corpus's dominant carrier IS family/role-tiered, matching the prior's dominant value, but the corpus also carries a substantial flat-namespace minority (X's path-null: 19/66=29%; Y's flat-namespace: 19/67=28%) that the prior's enum already names as a value ('flat') but never flagged as this prevalent -- the VALUE transfers, the WEIGHT the prior assigned it does not. (3) Tree depth 0-3+ -- the dominant shape sits at depth ~2-3 (matching prior's depth-3 dominant), but the flat-namespace population sits at depth 0-1, again within the enum's stated range but under-weighted by the prior's single dominant-cell claim. (4) generated-in-git yes/no/partial -- this is the CLEANEST fit: Y's independently-derived custody axis (committed-verified / excluded / durability-split) maps almost one-for-one onto the prior's yes/no/partial trichotomy, a striking corroboration that this trichotomy is a real, recurring, corpus-general fact rather than an artifact of the prior round's specific corpus. (5) Unit of description -- 'package' still dominates, but a meaningful minority (X's path-null elite X-seeded-35, several flat-namespace designs) EXPLICITLY redefines 'unit' as an abstract ownership/verification/delivery contract 'not necessarily an npm package' -- a genuine conceptual departure the prior's single assumed value ('package') did not anticipate as a named alternative. (6) Repo count -- trivially 1 in both rounds, no discriminating power. THE DECISIVE GAP: the prior tuple has NO axis at all corresponding to boundary-feedback/telemetry-governance -- the single most consequential NEW, non-schema-forced finding both X and Y converge on in this round (13/66-67, ~20%, carrying a measured falsifier). Y's own notes make the strongest version of this point directly: reusing something like the prior's descriptor tuple would have been largely NON-DISCRIMINATING on this corpus, because licence class, provenance, audience, trigger and assurance profile 'appear in nearly every one of the 67 designs' -- what actually varies here is path-load, byte-custody, and whether boundary revision is instrumented, and the prior tuple only glancingly touches the second of those three and misses the third entirely. VERDICT: the prior descriptor would have correctly classified the majority of this corpus into its known dominant cell, but it would have been blind to the corpus's most novel structural finding (the feedback-loop axis) and would have mis-predicted the relative weight of the flat/shallow minority -- an incomplete instrument for this corpus, not a wrong one."
comparator.notes: "Methodology: this is a pure textual/data analysis over the corpus supplied in the prompt -- no filesystem, git, or tool access was used or needed, since reductions X and Y, the 18 full baseline design records, and the 4 decoy outputs were all provided inline. Cell-membership arithmetic (basin mass, attractor-test shape assignments) was hand-verified against the literal memberIds arrays in each reduction's JSON rather than trusted from either reduction's own summary prose, per the estate's validators-must-recompute-not-just-record and verify-dont-trust practice -- several of the report's findings (the B-codex-12 contested placement, the K-fable-1-fix disagreement, the falsifier-basin-mass-is-flat-or-rising result) only surfaced BECAUSE the raw member lists were recomputed rather than the reductions' own headline claims taken at face value. Residual uncertainty, flagged rather than smoothed over: (a) six B2-* baseline designs (haiku-56, sonnet-57, opus-58, fable-59, codex-60, terra-61) have no raw design text in the supplied corpus data -- their attractor-test rows rest entirely on X's and Y's independent cell-placement agreement, which is corroborating but not independently verified against source, consistent with both landing them identically despite differing schemes; (b) the B-codex-12 case shows the underlying reduction instrument itself disagrees about a single design's primary classification, which should discount confidence in any report that treats either reduction's cell placement as ground truth for an individual design; (c) 'matchesDominant1aShape' required interpolating across X's 2-axis and Y's 3-axis schemes, since neither reduction natively answers a binary match/no-match question against the PRIOR round's shape -- this is a synthesis judgment, laid out with its reasoning in the attractor test verdict rather than asserted as a bare fact. No findings in this report rely on classification COUNT or carrier TYPE agreement between X and Y as evidence, per the task's explicit instruction that such agreement is schema-forced and uninformative."

boundaryFitness.evidence: S7 (vocab-mining/corpus-data, 95%) is NOT split: the design keeps oak-sdk-codegen as ONE sdk-tier unit that 'internally hosts all four Provenance kinds at once (authored generation code, two independently-triggered regenerated-cache collections...)' -- explicitly called 'the clearest demonstration that Tier and Provenance are independent axes' -- and P2 bundles 'vocab-gen output' inside that same unit as a sibling leaf. P7 (fidelity-capture, 86%) also stays one Audience=imported-evidence unit with no internal split named. But P10/S6 (es-ingest, 89%) IS split: 'Elasticsearch cluster-management machinery... currently living inside a product-audience app rather than promoted to lib tier' is confidently promoted OUT via the Coupling-Tier graduation rule ('the same graduation its sibling retrieval logic already received'), extracting ingest-pipeline machinery from its host with no cost check. Net: 2 of 3 measured high-co-change pairs preserved, 1 confidently violated.

governanceAnswerability.evidence: Four axes, four named single carriers per the design's own rules: Coupling Tier=directory depth; Audience & Support Promise=top-level directory; Artefact Provenance=fixed sub-directory naming + a license-field divergence flag; Shipment Membership=turbo.json task-input membership. Licence reads from the package.json license field alone; membership from the top-level directory alone; regeneration from the turbo outputs cross-checked against the provenance leaf name. Import direction is a single relative check (tier ordering against actual dependencies). Docked from 5 because the notes admit the enforcement scripts referenced (a 'validate-boundaries' script, a dependency-cruiser config) were seen only as filenames, never opened or confirmed -- classification is answerable from one place, but whether it's actually machine-checked is unverified by the design's own account.

boundaryFitness.evidence: S7's corpus mining stays one generation-namespace ('corpus mining to /generated/corpus'), with only cross-cutting orchestration split into a separate codegen-orchestrator tool that 'calls into the three generation-namespaces without holding their output itself' -- miner and mined data stay co-located, preserving the 95% pair. P7 stays one unitClass:research block. But P10 (89%, es-ingest) is placed at its stated target end-state as an extracted /packages/lib/generic/<name> unit, split from its host pipeline. It is marked forcedFit:true with an honest admission ('I have no enforcement instrument that DISCOVERS the mis-embedding before extraction'), but the actual recommended placement is still the split, so the 89% pair is violated.

governanceAnswerability.evidence: Each of the five axes reduces to one field plus one companion instrument: licence to the package.json license field; provenance (edit rights) AND regeneration both to a single provenance.json manifest per block ({kind, sourceEvent, stampHash}) -- usefully answering two of the five governance questions from one file; consumer-class/import-direction to a unitClass field read against one central dependency-cruiser/boundaries ruleset; live-reach to a touchesLiveSystems field; genericity to a generic field. Membership is the block/directory itself. No axis needs more than a field plus one central policy artefact to answer.

boundaryFitness.evidence: S7's mining is explicitly kept with its output: 'corpus mining -> unit corpus-miner (authored miner, 24MB derived corpus in .out/, never tracked)' -- the uniform-unit-anatomy rule puts the miner's own .out/ sink inside the SAME unit, preserving the 95% pair. P7 (study-evidence, one unit) keeps instrument and any derived findings inside that unit's src/ + .out/ split. But P10 (89%) is fully and unconditionally extracted: 'Extract to unit datastore-machinery declaring binds: []... The product-specific pipeline keeps a dependency edge on it' -- no cost-of-boundary reasoning is applied here even though the design's own quarterly co-change telemetry exists for exactly this decision.

governanceAnswerability.evidence: An explicit organising rule states 'classification-lives-in-manifest-only': all five policy axes (licence, support, gates, binds, provenance) sit in one strict estate block per unit's package.json, and 'uniform-unit-anatomy' makes every directory carry zero classification bits by rule. Licence, edit rights (provenance) and regeneration (derived[]/acquired[] entries) each read from exactly one manifest field; membership is the flat unit directory. Import direction is recomputed fresh each CI run from the graph against those same declared fields ('support-promise-flows-upstream... recomputed from the workspace graph every run (never recorded)') -- one live mechanism, not a stored/duplicated fact, which is a deliberate anti-staleness choice rather than a multi-carrier ambiguity.

boundaryFitness.evidence: S7 places the 24MB mined corpus inside ogl/curriculum-corpus/, and the design's own edit-ownership axis (every unit carries src/gen/vendor together) implies the miner code sits alongside it in the same ogl-rooted unit -- 'because the corpus is its own unit, moving 24MB times 19/yr out of git... touches zero imports and zero rules,' preserving the 95% pair, though the miner's exact co-location is inferred rather than stated as explicitly as in some peers. But P10 (89%) is fully extracted: 'Extracted as mit/datastore-kit/, with mit/search-cli/ depending on it' -- framed as a corrective improvement over the audited incumbent, but still an unconditional split of the measured ingest-pipeline pair.

boundaryFitness.evidence: S7's mining machinery is explicitly NOT extracted -- 'the mining machinery held as an entry point pending R3' -- staying inside internal/curriculum-corpus with its 24MB gen/ output; R0's trigger-based split rule assigns both the same corpus-mine trigger, so the 95% pair survives by principled construction, not accident. P7 stays one terminal/study-<name> unit under R7 ('a generated parcel lives in the unit whose script produces it'). But P10 (89%) is split immediately: 'if S6's retrieval library is the consumer that needs it, that is the second consumer and extraction fires now' -- R3's second-consumer threshold fires with no cost check, pulling datastore machinery out of its host pipeline.

governanceAnswerability.evidence: Edit rights (src/gen/vendor) and shipment/tier membership each read from one clean path segment; licence and change-trigger each read from one manifest field (license/oak.trigger), each with a consistent mirror (a LICENSE file, a repo policy-file enum) rather than an independent second fact. But import direction (R4) requires combining THREE separately declared facts -- channel (path), promise (manifest), and assurance (manifest, via the R6 monotonicity rule) -- plus a graph traversal, so 'who may depend on whom' cannot be read from one place. The design itself names a live gap: P12's failure-semantics distinction has no carrier among its five axes and is patched onto an entry-point field, an admitted incompleteness in the classification set itself.

boundaryFitness.evidence: The design's core rule structurally separates every generator from its generated output as a matter of principle -- P2: 'Shared generator logic, if any, occupies a separate human-authored library unit'; S5 splits token-source/compiler/generated-css into three units -- and 'Single contract shape' forbids one unit from declaring two contract kinds. Applied to S7, the S7 placement names 'corpus-miner executable or library' as a unit with no corresponding mined-data unit named alongside it; under the design's own single-contract-kind rule the 24MB mined output is structurally forced into a separate generated-artifact unit, violating the 95% vocab-mining/corpus-data pair by rule, not omission. P10 (89%) is also explicitly and fully split: 'Extract datastore-generic machinery into a datastore-machinery library unit... The product pipeline remains a separate unit.' The same rule makes it near-certain P7's capture instrument (library/executable) and its captured findings (dataset-typed) would split too, though that specific case is not spelled out in the P7 text.

governanceAnswerability.evidence: Every one of the five governance facts reads from exactly one place: estate.units.json. unit.controller (kind, producer, inputs, command, receipt) answers edit rights AND regeneration together; unit.rightsId answers licence via one foreign key into one shared rights table; unit.dir/unit.files answers membership; import direction is answered by the one generated estate.graph.json, combining static imports with declared generates/embeds/deploys-with/operates-on edges. The manifest 'explicitly enumerates every tracked file' with one field per fact type, the tightest single-source design of the seven.

boundaryFitness.evidence: S7 dissolves but the mining code and its 24MB mined output stay together inside one ogl-rooted unit, curriculum-corpus-ogl ('producer, mining trigger'), consistent with the materialisation rule that keeps a producer and its never-tracked derived output in the same unit's .out/ sink -- preserving the 95% pair. P7 gives the most explicit positive treatment of instrument+captured-output co-location of any of the seven designs: 'Its findings depend on corpus state at a moment in time, so... they are decision records and are tracked; its intermediate computations are reproducible... and are therefore never stored' -- both stay inside one search-quality-study unit. P10 (89%, es-ingest) gets the most measured answer in the corpus: only the piece 'that names the datastore SDK, endpoint or credential comes out now as search-cluster-adapter, because single-adapter is a hard rule,' while 'the remaining vendor-agnostic machinery stays inside search-retrieval until a second independent consumer appears, because a boundary costs cross-unit commits and there is currently one consumer' -- a genuine, evidence-priced partial preservation rather than a blind full extraction, though the adapter split is still a real, smaller violation of the pair.

governanceAnswerability.evidence: Assurance, exposure, provenance, materialisation (oak.produces[]) and external-touch (oak.externals[]) each read from one manifest field; membership is the flat units/<name> directory. Import legality (the strictness lattice, exposure closure) is recomputed fresh from the graph against those same declared fields -- one mechanism, never a stored duplicate. Docked from 5 because licence is signalled redundantly in three places at once -- 'oak.licence.{spdx,class}' manifest field, a LICENCE file, AND a name hazard token -- rather than a single carrier; the manifest is stated as canonical and the others as gate-checked mirrors, but the design itself calls this out as a deliberate exception rather than the norm.

scorer.notes:
Method: for each elite I read the actual design text (organisingRules "carrier" fields and the specific probePlacements for S7, P10, and P7, since the glosses map vocab-mining+corpus-data->S7's internals, es-ingest->P10/S6's world, fidelity-capture->P7's world) rather than the curator "whyElite" summaries in the reducer-cell JSON, which in at least one case (F-grade3-63) describe a path-partitioned scheme that contradicts the actual design text provided (a flat, manifest-only units/<name>/ namespace) -- I treated the full design text as authoritative per the instruction to score against the measured record, not prior characterisations.

Cross-design pattern on boundary fitness: every design in this elite set except O-grade3-62 gives an unconditional, no-cost-check extraction for P10 (the generic-datastore-machinery probe), which is exactly the case the 89% es-ingest co-change figure argues against. This looks like a systematic blind spot shared across otherwise very different organising principles (path-heavy, path-light, flat, tiered) -- the "extract generic-looking machinery on sight" instinct recurs regardless of framework, and only O-grade3-62 explicitly prices the boundary against the measured cross-unit-commit cost before deciding, and only for the credential-holding sliver rather than the whole machinery. X-seeded-35 additionally fails the vocab-mining/corpus-data pair by explicit, load-bearing rule (its "single contract shape" axiom forbids a generator and its own output from sharing a unit at all), which is a structural rather than incidental miss.

On governance answerability, the three designs built explicitly around "one fact, one carrier" as a named organising principle (K-opus-1-fix, X-seeded-35, F-grade3-63) score highest; designs whose import-direction rule requires combining two or three separately-declared facts before a graph check (B-opus-7 most notably) score lowest. I did not attempt to verify any design's enforcement machinery actually exists or runs -- several designs (S-seeded-26, O-grade3-62) explicitly flag that they saw only filenames suggesting enforcement scripts and never opened them, which I've reflected as a discount on confidence rather than a boundary-fitness or governance defect per se, since the scoring question is about classification answerability, not verified enforcement.

Loud branch: SOL-seeded-51's p.txt/s.json were overwritten with the D-decoy estate task mid-window; the relay agent detected the mutation and refused (result null, shortfall recorded) rather than transcribing it.
